profiles.name: MK-677 (ibutamoren)
profiles.molecularClass: Orally active nonpeptide small-molecule ghrelin-receptor agonist
profiles.summary: Ibutamoren is a nonpeptide drug candidate that stimulates growth hormone and IGF-1 through the ghrelin receptor. Human trials have examined aging, muscle loss, Alzheimer disease, and pediatric GH deficiency. Hormone and lean-mass increases have not consistently translated into functional benefit, and metabolic and heart-failure concerns remain.
profiles.description: Although often sold alongside peptides, MK-677 is a small molecule rather than an amino-acid chain. Oral activity helped make it attractive for long-term GH-secretagogue research. In older-adult trials it increased GH, IGF-1, and fat-free mass, but those changes did not establish improved strength or everyday function. A large Alzheimer disease trial found no clinical slowing despite clear IGF-1 increases. Development under the name LUM-201 continues in selected children with GH deficiency, including a registered phase 3 study. These distinct programs should not be merged into a general claim that ibutamoren treats aging or safely builds useful muscle.
profiles.mechanism: Ibutamoren activates the ghrelin receptor, stimulating hypothalamic–pituitary GH secretion and downstream IGF-1. Ghrelin signaling also influences appetite, and raising GH can reduce insulin sensitivity. The compound is therefore pharmacologically broader than an isolated muscle-building signal. Increased lean mass can include changes in body water and does not automatically represent stronger contractile tissue or improved physical performance.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Ibutamoren is not a peptide and is not an approved anti-aging treatment. It has substantial human research, including negative clinical outcomes and safety signals; ongoing pediatric development does not establish benefit for unsupervised adult physique use.

sections.title: Lean mass is not the same as physical benefit
sections.body: In a randomized study of 65 older adults, ibutamoren increased GH and fat-free mass without establishing a corresponding improvement in strength or function. Appetite, body weight, glucose, and insulin sensitivity also changed. The trial supports endocrine activity but not a claim of proven prevention of disability or age-related frailty.

sections.title: Negative outcomes and ongoing development
sections.body: A 563-participant Alzheimer trial found no slowing of clinical progression despite increased IGF-1. Separately, LUM-201 is being studied in children with GH deficiency in a registered phase 3 trial. An active study is evidence of development, not evidence that its endpoint has been met or that regulatory approval has been granted.

sections.title: Metabolic and cardiovascular concerns
sections.body: FDA identifies potential congestive heart failure risk, citing a hip-fracture recovery trial stopped early for a safety signal. Older-adult research also found reduced insulin sensitivity and increased fasting glucose. These findings are particularly relevant when marketing emphasizes muscle or recovery while omitting fluid balance, diabetes risk, and vulnerable patient groups.

sections.title: What is its current status?
sections.body: No FDA-approved ibutamoren medicine or anti-aging indication is established by these sources. FDA’s compounding review identifies significant safety concerns. LUM-201 trial participation, an internet research-product label, and a prescription from a clinic are different contexts and should not be described as equivalent evidence of product approval.

sections.title: Is ibutamoren actually a peptide?
sections.body: No. Ibutamoren is a small-molecule ghrelin-receptor agonist, despite frequently appearing in peptide catalogs. It stimulates the growth-hormone pathway but is not growth hormone itself. Its chemistry and ability to raise IGF-1 do not establish an approved treatment for aging, bodybuilding or athletic recovery.

profiles.name: Motixafortide
profiles.molecularClass: Cyclic peptide CXCR4 antagonist; hematopoietic stem-cell mobilizer
profiles.summary: Motixafortide is an approved stem-cell mobilization medicine used with filgrastim before autologous transplantation in multiple myeloma. It blocks CXCR4 so more hematopoietic stem cells enter the bloodstream for collection. This indication is distinct from experimental attempts to use CXCR4 blockade as cancer treatment.
profiles.description: Autologous stem-cell transplantation requires collection of enough of a patient’s own hematopoietic stem cells before high-dose therapy. Motixafortide helps release those cells from the bone-marrow environment when used with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, marketed as filgrastim. The US product Aphexda is approved for this mobilization purpose in multiple myeloma. Clinical outcomes in the pivotal program concerned successful cell collection within a limited number of apheresis procedures. They should not be described as proof that motixafortide directly treats myeloma or prolongs survival. Other oncology combinations involving the same pathway remain separate research questions with different endpoints and risk considerations.
profiles.mechanism: Motixafortide binds CXCR4 and inhibits its interaction with CXCL12, a chemokine signal that helps retain hematopoietic stem cells within marrow niches. Disrupting this signal increases circulating CD34-positive cells available for apheresis. CXCR4 also participates in other immune and tumor-cell processes, but that broad biology does not extend the approved indication automatically. Mobilizing malignant cells is one reason the intended transplant context matters.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Motixafortide has established evidence for improving stem-cell collection with filgrastim in multiple myeloma. Its approval concerns mobilization, while hypersensitivity, injection reactions, and possible tumor-cell mobilization require specific precautions.

atAGlance.label: Approved purpose
atAGlance.value: Stem-cell collection before autologous transplant in multiple myeloma

sections.title: Helping collect cells for transplantation
sections.body: The labeled use combines motixafortide with filgrastim to mobilize hematopoietic stem cells into peripheral blood for collection and subsequent autologous transplantation. This is a preparatory treatment within a transplant program. It is not an approved stand-alone anticancer therapy or a general method of stimulating regeneration in healthy people.

sections.title: What GENESIS demonstrated
sections.body: The randomized GENESIS trial compared motixafortide plus G-CSF with placebo plus G-CSF. A much larger proportion of treated participants collected the prespecified CD34-positive cell target within two apheresis procedures. This directly supports mobilization efficacy, but it does not independently establish longer survival or superior cancer control after transplantation.

sections.title: Hypersensitivity and cell-mobilization concerns
sections.body: The label warns about anaphylactic shock, hypersensitivity, injection-site reactions, leukocytosis, and potential mobilization of tumor cells. It specifically cautions against use for mobilization in leukemia because leukemic cells may enter circulation. Premedication and observation are part of the approved administration framework rather than evidence that reactions cannot occur.

sections.title: Does CXCR4 blockade make it an approved cancer immunotherapy?
sections.body: No. A molecular target can support several development programs, but each needs its own outcomes and authorization. Aphexda’s approval is tied to stem-cell collection in multiple myeloma. Experimental tumor-microenvironment studies and combinations cannot be presented as additional approved indications.

profiles.name: MOTS-c
aliases: Mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c
profiles.summary: MOTS-c is a mitochondrial-derived peptide studied in metabolic signaling and physical-function research. Experiments show effects in cells and mice, while observations of endogenous changes during human exercise do not establish that administering MOTS-c improves human health, performance or longevity.
profiles.description: The name refers to a short open reading frame associated with mitochondrial 12S rRNA. Discovery studies investigated its role in communication between mitochondrial metabolism and cellular responses. Later work reported better physical performance in treated mice and increased endogenous MOTS-c after exercise in people. These are different types of evidence: measuring a naturally occurring response in humans is not a treatment trial. FDA’s 2026 evaluation found major gaps in human exposure, pharmacokinetics and toxicology for proposed MOTS-c products. It remains a research compound rather than an approved metabolic or anti-aging medicine.
profiles.mechanism: The original research linked MOTS-c to changes in the folate cycle and purine synthesis, leading to AMPK-related metabolic signaling. Subsequent work explored nuclear gene regulation, muscle stress responses and metabolic adaptation. The precise molecular target remains incompletely defined. These pathways offer a biological hypothesis, but do not demonstrate that injected peptide reaches sustained active concentrations in human tissues or reproduces the effects of exercise.
profiles.keyTakeaway: MOTS-c is scientifically interesting mitochondrial signaling research, with a large gap between mouse treatment results and human therapeutic evidence. Exercise-associated measurements and compounding discussions do not fill that gap.

sections.title: Original metabolic experiments
sections.body: The discovery study reported prevention of age-related and diet-induced insulin resistance in mice, alongside cellular metabolic work. That supports the proposed signaling role without establishing a human obesity or diabetes treatment.

sections.title: Human observation versus mouse intervention
sections.body: A later study administered MOTS-c to mice and assessed physical performance. Its human component measured endogenous peptide changes after exercise. The human observation cannot be presented as evidence that MOTS-c injections improve exercise capacity in people.

sections.title: What FDA’s 2026 review identified
sections.body: The review found no adequate human administration data to characterize safety and highlighted missing pharmacokinetic and toxicology information. Rapid degradation in experimental human blood raised an additional exposure question. Unknown safety cannot be summarized as an absence of side effects.

sections.title: Compounding and approval are separate
sections.body: MOTS-c was discussed in the 2026 compounding advisory process. That process does not establish FDA approval of a medicine, an effective indication or a validated long-term regimen.

sections.title: Is this an exercise replacement?
sections.body: The evidence does not show that administering MOTS-c reproduces the broad effects of human physical activity. A pathway shared with exercise is a research lead, not proof that one peptide can replace training, nutrition or management of diagnosed metabolic disease.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Does exercise research prove that injecting MOTS-c improves human fitness? No. The cited work includes measurements of natural peptide responses in humans and administration experiments in mice; these are different types of evidence.

Does naturally occurring mean a marketed injectable is safe? No. Exogenous exposure, product identity, impurities, degradation and immune responses require direct assessment, and FDA identified substantial gaps in human safety information.

profiles.name: Murepavadin
profiles.summary: Murepavadin is an investigational antibiotic designed to target Pseudomonas aeruginosa through its outer-membrane assembly machinery. Intravenous phase 3 studies were terminated after safety review. Inhaled development is a separate program, and neither laboratory potency nor early tolerability establishes an approved treatment.
profiles.description: Murepavadin represents a pathogen-focused approach to antibiotic development. Instead of treating a broad range of organisms indiscriminately, it targets a bacterial outer-membrane protein important in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Early intravenous studies characterized human exposure and tolerability, followed by pneumonia trials in critically ill patients. The pivotal PRISM programs were stopped after safety concerns, including the renal signal described by the development program. Research then considered delivery directly to the lungs through inhalation. That route may change systemic exposure, but it requires its own evidence. Murepavadin remains distinct from approved polymyxin antibiotics despite being discussed alongside them in resistant-infection research.
profiles.mechanism: Murepavadin binds LptD, a protein involved in transporting lipopolysaccharide to the bacterial outer membrane. Disrupting that assembly pathway impairs membrane formation and bacterial survival. Its specificity for Pseudomonas biology distinguishes it from broadly membrane-disrupting polymyxins. An inhaled formulation aims to deliver active material to the respiratory tract, but local delivery does not automatically overcome all toxicity, distribution, or resistance challenges.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Murepavadin is a meaningful antibiotic-development candidate with an important failed intravenous program. Inhaled research must be assessed independently, and current evidence does not justify describing it as an approved or proven treatment for resistant pneumonia.

atAGlance.label: IV phase 3 history
atAGlance.value: PRISM studies terminated after safety review

sections.title: Early human studies were encouraging but incomplete
sections.body: A phase 1 study in healthy adults described intravenous pharmacokinetics and generally mild short-term adverse events. Such a study is useful for initial exposure characterization. It cannot predict all harms in critically ill pneumonia patients, whose kidney function, concurrent antibiotics, and illness severity differ substantially.

sections.title: Why the intravenous program matters
sections.body: ClinicalTrials.gov records for the pivotal pneumonia studies list termination after safety-data review. This is a material qualification to older articles describing murepavadin as simply in phase 3. Early tolerability and antibacterial activity did not settle the benefit–risk question in the intended patient population.

sections.title: The inhaled program asks a new question
sections.body: The iABC research consortium documents a completed phase 1 inhaled murepavadin study. The rationale is to characterize lung delivery and systemic exposure separately from intravenous use. A completed phase 1 study is not proof that exacerbations, bacterial eradication, lung function, or survival improve in bronchiectasis or cystic fibrosis.

sections.title: Is it a replacement for any antibiotic?
sections.body: No. Murepavadin’s narrow target makes pathogen identification particularly important, and no approved general substitution follows from its laboratory spectrum. Resistance, infection location, exposure, safety, and comparator therapy must all be addressed in clinical trials. Current research status should not be translated into an unsupervised antimicrobial use.

profiles.name: Nafarelin
profiles.molecularClass: Synthetic decapeptide GnRH agonist administered intranasally
profiles.summary: Nafarelin is an approved nasal GnRH-agonist medicine used for endometriosis and central precocious puberty. Continuous treatment suppresses pituitary-gonadal hormone signaling after an initial stimulation phase. Its nasal route does not make its systemic hormonal effects mild or purely local.
profiles.description: Nafarelin, marketed as Synarel, provides a noninjectable route for sustained suppression of reproductive hormone signaling. The US label covers central precocious puberty in children of either sex and management of endometriosis, including pain and lesions. The endometriosis experience described in the label is in adults treated for a limited course. Successful treatment depends on consistent absorption and follow-up, not merely possession of a nasal spray. Diagnosis is particularly important in children because early sexual development can have causes outside the central GnRH pathway, which require different investigation and treatment.
profiles.mechanism: Nafarelin stimulates pituitary GnRH receptors at first, briefly increasing gonadotropins and sex steroids. With repeated exposure, pituitary responsiveness declines, suppressing LH and FSH and lowering ovarian estrogen or testicular testosterone. This can reduce estrogen-driven endometriosis activity or pause premature central pubertal progression. The same mechanism can produce hot flushes, vaginal symptoms and bone effects, even though administration is through the nose.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Nafarelin is an established systemic hormone-suppressing medicine delivered by nasal spray. Its approved uses require diagnosis, monitoring and attention to treatment duration; nasal delivery does not remove GnRH-agonist risks or establish general fertility-enhancement benefits.

atAGlance.label: Mechanism-related concern
atAGlance.value: Reduced estrogen and bone mineral loss

sections.title: What conditions does the US label cover?
sections.body: For endometriosis, nafarelin is used to relieve pain and reduce lesions; the label describes experience in adults over a limited treatment course. For central precocious puberty, diagnosis requires evidence that the central reproductive pathway is active and exclusion of other causes of early development.

sections.title: What supports the endometriosis indication?
sections.body: A multicenter double-blind trial compared nasal nafarelin with oral danazol. Both treatments reduced endometriosis manifestations, with differing adverse-effect patterns. This evidence addresses treatment of established endometriosis rather than a claim that suppressing reproductive hormones improves fertility in people without that diagnosis.

sections.title: What should be assessed during treatment?
sections.body: The label addresses initial hormonal flare, loss of bone mineral density, pregnancy-related harm and hypersensitivity. Pediatric monitoring includes growth and biochemical suppression; warnings also cover psychiatric events, convulsions and intracranial hypertension. Nasal conditions and other intranasal medicines can affect practical administration and should be considered.

sections.title: Does lack of menstruation mean reliable contraception?
sections.body: No. Suppression of menstruation is a treatment effect, not assurance that pregnancy cannot occur. Nafarelin is contraindicated during pregnancy, and the label calls for appropriate pregnancy prevention. Likewise, an apparently convenient nasal route does not justify extending endometriosis treatment beyond the evidence and label limits.

profiles.name: Nangibotide
profiles.summary: Nangibotide is an investigational peptide designed to reduce excessive innate-immune signaling through the TREM-1 pathway. It has been studied in septic shock. The phase 2b ASTONISH trial did not meet its prespecified primary efficacy endpoint; biomarker subgroup findings remain hypotheses requiring confirmation.
profiles.description: Sepsis can involve harmful amplification of the host response to infection as well as inadequate immune function. Nangibotide was designed to modulate TREM-1-associated inflammatory amplification rather than act as an antibiotic. Clinical development has explored whether measuring soluble TREM-1 can identify patients most likely to respond. This is a precision-treatment hypothesis, not a validated general immune-balancing indication. The ASTONISH program provides substantial human research compared with many marketed research peptides, but its primary efficacy result was negative at the prespecified biomarker threshold. Later analyses with alternative thresholds should be presented as exploratory unless prospectively confirmed in a new controlled trial.
profiles.mechanism: Nangibotide is derived from a TREM-like transcript-1-related sequence and is intended to interfere with ligand-dependent activation of TREM-1. TREM-1 amplifies inflammatory signaling in myeloid immune cells, so modulation may reduce excessive host-response injury. The proposed effect is not direct bacterial killing. Because immune responses vary over the course of sepsis, identifying the appropriate biology and timing is central to the therapeutic hypothesis.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Nangibotide has real clinical development but no established approved sepsis role. ASTONISH’s missed primary endpoint and the exploratory nature of higher-biomarker subgroup findings are essential to a balanced description of its potential.

sections.title: What ASTONISH showed
sections.body: ASTONISH included 355 participants in its main analysis and compared two nangibotide regimens with placebo. The prespecified improvement in organ-failure score was not demonstrated at the selected soluble TREM-1 cutoff or in the overall population. Adverse-event frequencies were broadly similar, but the study did not establish a survival benefit.

sections.title: How should subgroup signals be read?
sections.body: An analysis using higher soluble TREM-1 thresholds suggested a larger organ-failure-score response in some participants. This may guide a future study, but selecting a different cutoff after examining results can create optimistic estimates. Prospective validation with a defined assay, threshold, population, and endpoint is needed before routine selection of patients is justified.

sections.title: The research setting limits generalization
sections.body: The trials involved closely monitored patients receiving standard sepsis care. Similar event rates between trial arms do not establish the safety of outpatient immune modulation, chronic exposure, or use with a different infection. Sepsis itself produces many serious events, making both attribution and adequate comparator groups important.

sections.title: Would it replace antibiotics or resuscitation?
sections.body: No. The intervention was investigated as an addition to established septic-shock care, not as a substitute for infection treatment or organ support. Its proposed action concerns the host response. No FDA-approved general immunity, inflammation, or anti-aging indication can be inferred from this research program.

profiles.name: Nesiritide
profiles.summary: Nesiritide is recombinant human B-type natriuretic peptide, historically approved for acutely decompensated heart failure. It lowers cardiac filling pressures through vasodilation. A large trial did not show improved death or readmission outcomes, and Natrecor’s US approval was withdrawn in 2020 after commercial discontinuation.
profiles.description: Nesiritide reproduces a hormone released by the heart in response to increased wall stress. The intravenous product Natrecor was developed to reduce congestion-related hemodynamic abnormalities and breathlessness in hospitalized heart failure. Initial studies supported short-term pressure and symptom effects, but later large-scale outcomes research changed its place in practice. ASCEND-HF did not establish a meaningful advantage for death or rehospitalization and found more hypotension. FDA subsequently withdrew the Natrecor application at the sponsor’s request because the product was no longer marketed. Its historical approval should therefore not be displayed as if it remained a currently available routine US heart-failure treatment.
profiles.mechanism: Nesiritide activates natriuretic peptide receptors linked to guanylyl cyclase and increases cyclic GMP. This relaxes vascular smooth muscle, reduces preload and afterload, and can influence renal sodium handling. Hemodynamic effects may relieve congestion but can also lower systemic pressure excessively. A favorable change in filling pressure does not by itself establish improved kidney outcomes, fewer admissions, or longer survival.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Nesiritide illustrates the difference between improving short-term hemodynamics and improving clinical outcomes. Its large trial was neutral on death and readmission, hypotension increased, and the discontinued US product’s approval has been withdrawn.

sections.title: The original approved role
sections.body: The historical label covered acutely decompensated heart failure with breathlessness at rest or minimal activity. It described reduced pulmonary capillary wedge pressure and short-term symptomatic improvement. The product was administered intravenously under close blood-pressure monitoring, rather than as a chronic outpatient strategy for preventing heart-failure progression.

sections.title: What ASCEND-HF clarified
sections.body: In the large ASCEND-HF randomized trial, nesiritide did not significantly reduce death or heart-failure rehospitalization. Its effect on breathlessness did not meet the prespecified significance threshold, and hypotension occurred more often. The study did not confirm the earlier concern of significantly worse renal outcomes, but it also did not establish renal protection.

sections.title: Blood pressure was a central limitation
sections.body: The label contraindicated use with persistent low systolic pressure and cardiogenic shock and warned about hypotension, renal impairment, and hypersensitivity. A vasodilator can reduce filling pressure while compromising perfusion in a vulnerable patient. That competing effect is why hemodynamic monitoring and patient selection were integral to its historical use.

sections.title: Is Natrecor still an approved US product?
sections.body: FDA’s Federal Register notice lists Natrecor among applications withdrawn effective June 15, 2020, after sponsors reported that the products were no longer marketed. This administrative history should be distinguished from a claim that the hormone has no biological activity. The old label remains a historical source, not evidence of current availability.

sections.title: Did improving filling pressure prove better survival?
sections.body: No. A favorable short-term hemodynamic effect is not equivalent to improved clinical outcomes. ASCEND-HF did not establish reduced death or heart-failure rehospitalization and found more hypotension. The history of nesiritide shows why symptom, physiological and outcome endpoints must be reported separately.

profiles.name: NNZ-2591
profiles.summary: NNZ-2591 is an investigational oral compound in development for rare neurodevelopmental syndromes. An early open-label Phelan-McDermid study reported improvements, but its uncontrolled design cannot establish efficacy. It is distinct from trofinetide despite their related development background.
profiles.description: NNZ-2591 is modeled on cyclic glycine-proline, a metabolite associated with insulin-like growth factor 1 biology. It is being developed for conditions with substantial developmental and behavioral needs, including Phelan-McDermid syndrome. These are disease-specific programs, not evidence for general cognitive enhancement. The published phase 2 Phelan-McDermid study provides useful information about exposure, short-term tolerability, and possible outcome measures. However, all participants received active treatment. Caregiver expectation, natural variation, and changes in support can influence observed improvement when there is no concurrent placebo group. Controlled studies are therefore an essential next step.
profiles.mechanism: The development hypothesis involves modulation of IGF-1-related signaling and downstream processes affecting neuronal development and connectivity. NNZ-2591 is an analog of cyclic glycine-proline, whereas trofinetide is an analog of glycine-proline-glutamate. That chemical distinction matters: one compound’s approval and trial outcomes cannot be transferred to the other. The exact connection between proposed signaling effects and meaningful functional benefit remains under clinical investigation.
profiles.keyTakeaway: NNZ-2591 has early human research and ongoing clinical development, but uncontrolled improvement is not proof of treatment efficacy. Trofinetide approval, orphan designations, and trial authorization do not amount to approval of NNZ-2591.

sections.title: What the published phase 2 study shows
sections.body: Eighteen children with Phelan-McDermid syndrome received NNZ-2591 in a 13-week open-label study. Several secondary efficacy assessments improved from baseline, and most reported adverse events were mild or moderate. Safety and pharmacokinetics were primary objectives. Multiple secondary outcomes and the small uncontrolled sample make these signals preliminary rather than confirmatory.

sections.title: Current development context
sections.body: Neuren uses ercanetide as another name for NNZ-2591 and reported initiation of the randomized phase 3 Koala program in Phelan-McDermid syndrome in 2026. The program is designed to resolve uncertainties that an open-label study cannot. A sponsor report establishes the developer’s program description, not independent confirmation that eventual results will be positive.

sections.title: Avoid double-counting publications
sections.body: The 2026 publication with DOI ending 0200405 is an erratum to the phase 2 article, not another clinical trial. A correction to one report should not be mistaken for an additional trial or independent replication of the original findings. Long-term safety also remains a separate question from short-term tolerability.

profiles.name: Nonapeptide-1
profiles.summary: Nonapeptide-1 is a cosmetic research ingredient associated with skin-pigmentation claims. Cell experiments examine interference with alpha-MSH-related melanogenesis. That mechanistic evidence does not establish reliable treatment of melasma or durable lightening from a particular consumer product.
profiles.description: Nonapeptide-1 is a nine-residue peptide used in research on the signaling that controls melanin production. The acetate form appears in published cell experiments. Its presence as a cosmetic ingredient should be distinguished from a prescription treatment for a pigment disorder. Skin pigmentation is influenced by several cell types, ultraviolet exposure, inflammation, and hormonal factors; a favorable result in one signaling pathway does not resolve all of those contributors. Its pigmentation-related research rationale is scientifically relevant, while the evidence supporting visible benefit in people remains much less developed. Laboratory activity is relevant, but direct controlled human outcomes remain the missing link for broad efficacy claims.
profiles.mechanism: The research rationale involves antagonism of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating-hormone signaling at the melanocortin-1 receptor. In a study primarily investigating tea polyphenols, nonapeptide-1 acetate was used as a pathway-related comparator and influenced melanogenesis-associated measurements. This supports a laboratory role in the pathway, but does not demonstrate the exposure, magnitude, persistence, or safety of an effect after ordinary topical application.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Nonapeptide-1 has pigmentation-pathway evidence in cells, not established clinical proof for a general skin-lightening treatment. A study using it as an experimental comparator should not be promoted as a human efficacy trial.

sections.title: What the cited experiment actually studied
sections.body: The 2022 paper focused on tea polyphenols and used human keratinocytes and melanocytes exposed to UVA. Nonapeptide-1 acetate was included in comparator and combination conditions. The investigators measured melanin, tyrosinase-related activity, and signaling proteins. These are cell-culture endpoints; the paper did not enroll people with dark spots or test a finished cosmetic cream.

sections.title: Do not transfer the paper’s headline conclusion
sections.body: Results attributed to tea polyphenols or a combination cannot all be attributed to nonapeptide-1. Likewise, lower melanin in a controlled cell system does not show how a peptide crosses intact skin or whether visible benefit lasts. A clinical study would need an appropriate vehicle control, standardized photography or color measurement, and follow-up.

sections.title: Pigmentation claims need a defined scope
sections.body: Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. The available experiment does not establish long-term tolerability, use on all skin types, or treatment of a medical pigment disorder. Appearance-related product claims should remain specific to tested formulations, without treating the ingredient name or pathway rationale as an approval.

profiles.name: Octreotide
profiles.summary: Octreotide suppresses several endocrine and gastrointestinal secretions and is an established treatment for acromegaly and hormone-driven symptoms of selected neuroendocrine tumors. Evidence and approved uses depend on the formulation, with short-acting injections, depot products and other presentations serving different clinical roles.
profiles.description: Sandostatin injection is approved for reducing GH and IGF-1 in selected patients with acromegaly, severe diarrhea and flushing associated with metastatic carcinoid tumors, and watery diarrhea from VIP-secreting tumors. Long-acting formulations provide sustained exposure for appropriate patients. Symptom suppression can be valuable even when it does not mean the underlying tumor has disappeared. Octreotide is also studied and used in other specialist settings, but those practices must be distinguished from the specific product label. One formulation’s indication or administration method should never be assumed to apply to every octreotide product.
profiles.mechanism: Octreotide binds somatostatin receptors and reproduces many effects of the body’s inhibitory hormone somatostatin. It suppresses GH, insulin, glucagon and several gastrointestinal peptides, and can reduce splanchnic blood flow. These actions explain both control of hormone-mediated diarrhea and important off-target effects on glucose, gallbladder emptying and digestion. Its receptor profile and duration differ from other somatostatin analogs.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Octreotide has established disease-specific uses, but controlling hormone symptoms and controlling tumor growth are different objectives. The actual formulation, disease and monitoring plan determine how its evidence applies.

sections.title: Label-specific uses
sections.body: The injectable Sandostatin label emphasizes endocrine and symptom control. It explicitly distinguishes those findings from evidence of tumor shrinkage or slowed growth in its original trials. Other formulations and studies should be evaluated separately.

sections.title: Antiproliferative evidence
sections.body: PROMID evaluated long-acting octreotide in metastatic midgut neuroendocrine tumors and found longer time to tumor progression than placebo. This is evidence for a defined tumor population and formulation, not proof that short-acting octreotide treats all cancers.

sections.title: Important adverse effects
sections.body: Gallstones and their complications, bradycardia, arrhythmias and conduction abnormalities can occur. Insulin and glucagon suppression can produce either high or low glucose. Hypothyroidism and gastrointestinal adverse effects are also recognized.

sections.title: Digestive symptoms during treatment
sections.body: New greasy stools, stool discoloration, loose stools, bloating or weight loss may reflect pancreatic exocrine insufficiency. These symptoms can resemble the underlying gastrointestinal disease, making reassessment important rather than automatically assuming the original illness has worsened.

sections.title: Why formulation matters
sections.body: An immediate-acting injection, long-acting depot and an oral formulation have different absorption and exposure. They are not interchangeable based on the ingredient name alone. The chosen product determines the relevant indication, administration and follow-up instructions.

profiles.name: Oligopeptide-1
profiles.summary: Oligopeptide-1 appears in cosmetic products and research associated with epidermal growth factor. Exact ingredient identity and formulation require attention. Small product-comparison studies do not establish that every similarly named growth-factor serum has the same composition, penetration, or clinical effect.
profiles.description: The label oligopeptide-1 is used in an EGF-related cosmetic context, including a recent study describing its test serum as recombinant epidermal growth factor. For accurate interpretation, the ingredient specification matters: naming conventions, source, sequence, and manufacturing can differ among products marketed under growth-factor language. A conditioned-media product containing multiple biological components is also different from a defined recombinant ingredient. Products described with similar EGF terminology should therefore not be assumed chemically or clinically equivalent without examining their specifications and direct comparative evidence. The relevant question is what a particular tested serum changed in human skin appearance, and whether the design can identify the responsible ingredient.
profiles.mechanism: EGF-related research concerns signaling through the epidermal-growth-factor receptor, which influences cellular growth and repair responses. A plausible receptor pathway does not establish that a cosmetic formulation delivers an active molecule through intact skin to the necessary location. Growth-factor signaling also cannot simply be described as universally beneficial. Product identity, exposure, and the specific clinical outcome remain essential to interpreting proposed rejuvenation effects.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Oligopeptide-1 should be understood through the exact product specification and study. Limited growth-factor serum comparisons do not establish universal anti-aging efficacy, equivalence between sources, or an approved injectable or wound-treatment role.

atAGlance.label: Identity requirement
atAGlance.value: Verify sequence, source, and complete formulation

sections.title: A recent randomized pilot
sections.body: A 2026 blinded pilot randomized twenty women to an oligopeptide-1/recombinant-EGF-context serum or a human-derived conditioned-media serum for twelve weeks. Some investigator-rated texture and firmness outcomes favored the former, while global wrinkle ratings changed little. The small sample and comparison of two multi-component products limit broad conclusions about isolated EGF efficacy.

sections.title: What the design cannot establish
sections.body: The pilot did not compare a purified peptide against an otherwise identical vehicle, and the participants were predominantly White women with a limited range of skin types. It therefore cannot establish equivalent outcomes for all products, skin types, or age groups. A product-level difference is not proof that the named growth factor alone caused it.

sections.title: Avoid expanding the claim beyond the study
sections.body: Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. Short-term facial tolerability does not establish long-term effects of growth-factor exposure, application to disrupted skin, or injection. An ingredient listing should not be used to imply approved treatment of ulcers, scars, or other medical conditions without separate product-specific evidence.

profiles.name: Oxytocin
profiles.molecularClass: Cyclic nonapeptide hormone and uterotonic medicine
profiles.summary: Oxytocin is a naturally occurring nine-amino-acid hormone and an established obstetric medicine. Approved injectable products help initiate or strengthen suitable labor contractions and control postpartum uterine bleeding. Claims about routine enhancement of bonding, mood or social behavior require separate evidence.
profiles.description: Natural oxytocin participates in uterine contraction and milk ejection, while pharmaceutical oxytocin is used in monitored maternity care for specific obstetric purposes. The US injectable label includes medically indicated labor induction, selected augmentation of labor, adjunctive management of incomplete or inevitable abortion, and production of uterine contractions to control postpartum bleeding. Appropriate use depends on maternal and fetal assessment and whether vaginal delivery is suitable. Intranasal oxytocin investigated for behavioral or psychiatric effects is a separate research context; the established obstetric record does not automatically validate those applications or an unapproved compounded formulation.
profiles.mechanism: Oxytocin activates oxytocin receptors on uterine smooth-muscle cells, engaging intracellular signaling that increases calcium and promotes contraction. Uterine sensitivity varies with pregnancy and clinical context. After delivery, contraction helps compress uterine blood vessels and limit bleeding. At higher or prolonged exposure, oxytocin’s antidiuretic activity can also influence water balance, contributing to the risk of water intoxication and low sodium.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Oxytocin has established obstetric uses with substantial monitoring needs. Evidence for labor and postpartum bleeding should remain separate from experimental intranasal or behavioral uses, where a natural-hormone mechanism has not consistently translated into clinical benefit.

sections.title: Where is oxytocin established?
sections.body: The injectable label describes medically indicated induction or reinforcement of suitable labor and control of postpartum uterine bleeding. It also includes adjunctive management of incomplete or inevitable abortion. Suitability depends on the obstetric situation; circumstances requiring surgical delivery or making vaginal delivery unsafe are important contraindications.

sections.title: Does the obstetric evidence prove behavioral benefit?
sections.body: No. A 24-week placebo-controlled trial in 290 children and adolescents with autism found no significant advantage for intranasal oxytocin on the primary social-withdrawal measure. This result does not erase oxytocin’s obstetric utility; it shows that effects depend on route, population and clinical outcome.

sections.title: Why is monitoring essential?
sections.body: Excessive uterine activity can compromise fetal oxygenation and can cause serious maternal injury, including uterine rupture. Prolonged administration can cause water intoxication, hyponatremia and seizures. Appropriate assessment of contractions, fetal status, fluid balance and the overall maternal condition is fundamental to safe clinical use.

sections.title: Is a “bonding hormone” label a treatment indication?
sections.body: No. A hormone’s physiological role does not establish that administering it improves relationships, sexual function, mood or social behavior. Those questions require their own controlled studies and product-specific evaluation. Approved injectable oxytocin for obstetric care should not be presented as approval of intranasal wellness products.

profiles.name: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12
profiles.summary: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 is a cosmetic peptide based on an elastin-related sequence. Recent research examines its self-assembly and interaction with excised human skin. These material and tissue findings do not establish that ordinary consumer products rebuild elastin or reverse skin aging.
profiles.description: This ingredient attaches a palmitoyl group to the sequence valine-glycine-valine-alanine-proline-glycine. The fatty-acid modification influences how the molecule behaves in formulations and interacts with skin structures. It is often discussed as an elastin-related signaling peptide, but newer research also considers its physical self-assembly into organized structures. Those are distinct possible explanations for measured effects. A change in skin mechanics or water distribution can occur without proving production of new functional elastic fibers in living people. Molecular identity and experimental tissue measurements are well-defined research questions, while direct clinical evidence for specific visible outcomes remains considerably more limited.
profiles.mechanism: A 2025 study tracked palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 in human skin layers and examined how it self-assembles and interacts with native skin components. Such work suggests possible physical effects on barrier properties and hydration alongside traditional signaling hypotheses. It does not show that the ingredient acts as replacement elastin. The behavior of a particular sol or gel preparation also cannot be assumed for every cream containing it.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 has interesting skin-material research, but ex vivo penetration and mechanical measurements are not a clinical anti-aging outcome. Claims should stay tied to the tested preparation and distinguish physical effects from new tissue synthesis.

sections.title: What the 2025 study adds
sections.body: Researchers used chemical imaging and mechanical methods to track the peptide in skin layers and examine its interactions with tissue components. They reported penetration into stratum-corneum and epidermal regions and changes in a deliberately altered barrier model. This is direct experimental work, but not a randomized facial trial or evidence of long-term wrinkle reduction.

sections.title: Why sequence and preparation matter
sections.body: The CIR assessment identifies the palmitoylated hexapeptide and distinguishes it from unmodified hexapeptide-12 and other peptide derivatives. Altering the lipid group, sequence, or physical formulation changes the material being tested. A general peptide label cannot preserve those distinctions on its own.

sections.title: Scope of a cosmetic assessment
sections.body: Cosmetic safety assessments concern described topical practices, not systemic injection or unlimited use. Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. The recent experimental findings should motivate product-specific testing of tolerability and appearance outcomes rather than an unsupported claim that all elastin-related benefits have been clinically demonstrated.

profiles.name: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4
profiles.summary: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 is a cosmetic signaling peptide associated with the original Matrixyl ingredient. A controlled split-face trial supports some improvement in photoaged facial appearance. It is a different ingredient from the two-peptide Matrixyl 3000 blend and from Matrixyl synthe’6.
profiles.description: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 links a fatty-acid chain to the five-amino-acid sequence lysine-threonine-threonine-lysine-serine, usually shortened to KTTKS. Research on that sequence began with extracellular-matrix signaling in cultured cells. Adding the palmitoyl group changes the molecule’s formulation properties and distinguishes the cosmetic ingredient from the unmodified peptide. The human evidence is stronger than a supplier claim alone because a randomized, blinded, vehicle-controlled study exists. Even so, a successful study of one moisturizer does not establish equal performance in every serum, permanent reversal of aging, or a treatment for scars and wounds.
profiles.mechanism: KTTKS is a fragment associated with type I procollagen and has been studied as a signal influencing matrix production. Original cell experiments found effects on collagen and fibronectin synthesis. Palmitoylation was used to adapt the peptide for topical cosmetic formulation. The resulting concept is a signaling ingredient, not replacement collagen physically filling the dermis; penetration and final-product composition still determine what exposure is achieved.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 has a relevant controlled cosmetic study, but its evidence remains product-specific. Keep original Matrixyl separate from Matrixyl 3000 and synthe’6 so that trial results are not transferred between different ingredients.

sections.title: The split-face trial
sections.body: A 12-week double-blind study in 93 women compared a moisturizer containing pal-KTTKS with the same vehicle on the other side of the face. Technical image analysis and expert grading found improvement in fine lines and wrinkles relative to the control. The matching vehicle is a strength because it helps separate peptide-associated effects from ordinary moisturization.

sections.title: Cell findings support a rationale, not every claim
sections.body: The original KTTKS study examined extracellular-matrix production in cultured mesenchymal cells. It helps explain why the sequence was investigated, but does not prove systemic repair or effects on all skin structures. The human cosmetic trial is the more direct evidence for visible facial outcomes.

sections.title: Interpret the finished formulation
sections.body: The clinical formulation was described as well tolerated, but that does not establish zero irritation with all products or unlimited exposure. Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. Brand-family similarity should not obscure that other Matrixyl products contain different peptides and require their own evidence.

profiles.name: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7
profiles.summary: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 is one of the two peptide actives in Matrixyl 3000 and appears in other cosmetic blends. Much of the human evidence concerns complete multi-ingredient products. It cannot determine how much benefit comes from this peptide alone.
profiles.description: The ingredient consists of the four-residue sequence glycine-glutamine-proline-arginine linked to a palmitoyl group. It is chemically distinct from its frequent companion palmitoyl tripeptide-1. Pairing them in a commercial complex may be useful for formulation, but it creates an evidence-attribution problem: an improved finished product does not reveal the contribution of each peptide. The two molecules retain different chemical identities even when formulated together, so their shared blend context cannot establish identical biological activity or independent efficacy. Marketing language about matrix repair or age reversal should be interpreted as a claim requiring specific outcome data, rather than a consequence automatically proven by the ingredient’s structure.
profiles.mechanism: The peptide is marketed within a matrikine-style signaling concept, with proposed effects on inflammatory or matrix-related cellular responses. Its GQPR sequence is described in the CIR assessment as related to an immunoglobulin fragment. That structural relationship is not proof of a clinically useful anti-inflammatory action. Human evidence needs to distinguish the isolated peptide from companion actives and from the moisturizing properties of the formulation.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 is a distinct ingredient often tested within blends. Preserve that identity, but attribute observed benefits to the tested product unless a controlled design isolates this peptide’s contribution.

sections.title: The finished-product evidence
sections.body: A 2024 study examined an eye cream combining these two palmitoylated peptides with a fermentation filtrate and N-acetylneuraminic acid. It included fibroblast experiments and a twelve-week human evaluation. The results concern that complete intervention. They cannot demonstrate that palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 alone produced changes in hydration, elasticity, or collagen-related measurements.

sections.title: What Matrixyl 3000 documentation establishes
sections.body: Croda’s documentation confirms that Matrixyl 3000 contains both palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7. It also reports supplier efficacy claims. The composition is useful factual information, while the claims require appraisal of the underlying design and replication. The ingredient blend is not a single peptide with two interchangeable names.

sections.title: Keep topical assessment separate from approval
sections.body: The CIR assessment covers described cosmetic uses of this ingredient family. It does not demonstrate an injected therapeutic effect. Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. Product tolerability and the strength of the specific appearance claim still need to be assessed for the finished formulation.

profiles.name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1
profiles.summary: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 is a lipid-modified GHK peptide used in cosmetics, including Matrixyl 3000. It is not copper tripeptide-1. Published findings often involve combined formulations, so the isolated ingredient’s contribution to visible skin improvement remains uncertain.
profiles.description: This ingredient links palmitic acid to glycine-histidine-lysine. The modification changes the molecule from unbound GHK and from the copper complex GHK-Cu. Those related names are easy to confuse, but evidence cannot move between them without justification. Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 commonly appears alongside palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 in a commercial blend and with multiple other actives in finished products. Its proposed role is signaling rather than supplying bulk collagen to fill the skin. The relevant question is whether a defined topical product improves a measured outcome beyond its vehicle, and whether any improvement can specifically be assigned to this peptide.
profiles.mechanism: The cosmetic rationale is based on a matrix-fragment signaling concept associated with the GHK sequence, with palmitoylation used to modify formulation behavior. That does not establish identical activity to GHK-Cu, since copper coordination and lipid attachment are different chemical changes. Penetration, stability, and the surrounding formulation determine exposure. A theoretical collagen-related signal therefore needs direct confirmation in the final product and population.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 differs chemically from GHK-Cu and from its frequent companion palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7. Product-level improvements can be informative, but they do not prove the independent effect of every peptide on the ingredient list.

atAGlance.value: Most human data concern complete formulations

sections.title: A relevant multi-component eye-cream study
sections.body: A 2024 publication evaluated an active complex containing palmitoyl tripeptide-1, palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, fermentation filtrate, and N-acetylneuraminic acid. Laboratory and twelve-week human measurements supported further investigation of the formula. The design cannot assign the outcome solely to palmitoyl tripeptide-1 or establish the same performance in an unrelated serum.

sections.title: Why the copper distinction matters
sections.body: The CIR document describes palmitoyl tripeptide-1 as lipid-modified GHK, while copper tripeptide-1 is a metal complex. A study of one should not automatically populate the other’s benefit claims. The same rule applies to Matrixyl 3000: its two peptides remain distinct molecules even when sold together.

sections.title: Read safety in the correct context
sections.body: Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. The ingredient-family assessment concerns described topical practices, not injected use. Whole-product irritation, stability, and formulation compatibility remain relevant, and absence of a serious event in a small cosmetic study cannot establish unlimited or long-term safety.

profiles.name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38
profiles.summary: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38 is the peptide associated with Matrixyl synthe’6. Supplier claims concern several extracellular-matrix components. A published human study tested it with vitamins C and E, so that study cannot establish the peptide’s independent contribution to changes in facial appearance.
profiles.description: This ingredient belongs to a family of lipid-modified cosmetic peptides, but its identity differs from original Matrixyl and the Matrixyl 3000 blend. The number in the ingredient name is part of the identifier, not a ranking of potency. The supplier promotes a matrix-related rationale involving multiple skin constituents. That claim should be assessed alongside the evidence design rather than treated as six independently demonstrated clinical benefits. Human research on a serum combining the peptide with antioxidants can be relevant to the final product, while still leaving the separate value of each component unresolved. The same distinction applies to brand-family comparisons.
profiles.mechanism: The proposed mechanism involves signaling associated with extracellular-matrix and dermal-epidermal-junction components. Croda describes effects on six matrix-related constituents in its supplier material. Those laboratory or supplier observations are not equivalent to demonstrating that a consumer serum rebuilds all those structures in living skin. A formulation containing strong co-actives requires an appropriate component-control design to isolate any peptide-specific mechanism.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Palmitoyl tripeptide-38 has supplier and combination-product evidence, not definitive isolated-ingredient proof. Keep Matrixyl synthe’6 distinct from other Matrixyl ingredients and interpret published cosmetic outcomes at the level of the serum actually studied.

atAGlance.value: Serum containing vitamins C and E

sections.title: What the serum study found
sections.body: A 2020 open-label study followed women using a serum containing ascorbic acid, tocopheryl acetate, and palmitoyl tripeptide-38 for 56 days. Instrumental roughness measurements and participant perceptions improved. Without a matched control and separate component comparisons, the study cannot determine how much change was due to the peptide, antioxidants, moisturizer vehicle, or expectation.

sections.title: One brand family, different ingredients
sections.body: The manufacturer lists palmitoyl tripeptide-38 in Matrixyl synthe’6. Original Matrixyl contains palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, while Matrixyl 3000 combines different peptides. Their studies should remain linked to the correct ingredient or blend; similar packaging or names do not make their molecular evidence interchangeable.

sections.title: Cosmetic use is a bounded claim
sections.body: Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. Short-term tolerability of an antioxidant serum does not establish injection safety or universal suitability of all formulations. Evidence should focus on the actual appearance endpoint and product tested, rather than converting matrix-related marketing language into a medical regeneration claim.

profiles.name: Palopegteriparatide
profiles.summary: Palopegteriparatide is an approved hormone-replacement medicine for adults with hypoparathyroidism. Its prodrug design releases active PTH over time to help regulate calcium and phosphate. The treatment can reduce dependence on conventional supplements, but both high and low calcium remain important risks.
profiles.description: Hypoparathyroidism involves inadequate parathyroid hormone activity, often after neck surgery, with consequences for blood calcium, phosphate, and kidney handling of minerals. Palopegteriparatide provides sustained exposure to the active N-terminal PTH fragment through a cleavable carrier. Yorvipath received US approval for adults with this disorder. The therapeutic objective is physiologic mineral regulation rather than osteoporosis treatment or nonspecific bone growth. Trials assessed whether participants could maintain normal calcium while becoming independent of active vitamin D and substantial calcium supplementation. The product is distinct from full-length PTH(1–84) and from intermittent teriparatide used in osteoporosis, even though their active signaling pathways overlap.
profiles.mechanism: After injection, the prodrug gradually releases PTH(1–34), which activates PTH1 receptors in kidney and bone. PTH promotes renal calcium retention, phosphate excretion, and formation of active vitamin D, helping restore the endocrine control missing in hypoparathyroidism. Sustained delivery is central to the design; it cannot be assumed that a brief injection of another PTH product reproduces the same exposure or clinical effects.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Palopegteriparatide is a current approved replacement option for adult hypoparathyroidism. Its value is restoring mineral control and reducing supplement burden, with careful monitoring because treatment changes or interruptions can cause serious calcium disturbances.

sections.title: Hormone replacement for hypoparathyroidism
sections.body: Yorvipath is approved for adult hypoparathyroidism. The label does not establish its use for acute postsurgical hypoparathyroidism, and studied participants had stabilized calcium before treatment. Clinicians assess current supplements and mineral results together because improving PTH activity changes the amount of calcium and active vitamin D needed.

sections.title: What the pivotal trial measured
sections.body: The PaTHway program used a combined endpoint: calcium within the normal range together with independence from active vitamin D and therapeutic calcium supplementation. More participants receiving palopegteriparatide reached this endpoint than placebo recipients. This is evidence of mineral-control benefit, not proof that every long-term kidney or skeletal complication is prevented.

sections.title: Calcium changes and other precautions
sections.body: Serious hypercalcemia and hypocalcemia can require hospitalization, particularly during adjustment or abrupt interruption. Other issues include hypersensitivity, postural hypotension, and increased digoxin toxicity when calcium rises. PTH-class osteosarcoma precautions apply to patients with elevated baseline risk; the warning should not be translated into a claim of proven human cancer causation.

sections.title: Is it the same as Natpara or teriparatide?
sections.body: No. Natpara contains full-length PTH(1–84); teriparatide contains PTH(1–34) without this sustained-release prodrug system. Yorvipath has its own approved indication, device, exposure pattern, and clinical evidence. Shared PTH receptor activity does not make these products interchangeable or establish equivalence for compounded versions.

profiles.name: Parathyroid hormone
profiles.summary: Parathyroid hormone regulates calcium and phosphate through kidney and bone signaling. Full-length recombinant PTH(1–84) was approved as Natpara for selected patients with hypoparathyroidism. Manufacturing ended after persistent supply problems, so its historical approval must be distinguished from current treatment availability.
profiles.description: Natural PTH is released by the parathyroid glands when blood calcium falls. This entry focuses on the full-length 84-amino-acid hormone and the recombinant medicine Natpara, rather than the separately listed PTH fragments and prodrugs. Natpara was approved as an adjunct to calcium and vitamin D for hypocalcemia in hypoparathyroidism when conventional treatment was inadequate. The product subsequently faced a US recall and prolonged supply constraints. Takeda announced global manufacturing discontinuation at the end of 2024 and no US re-commercialization. Consequently, a directory entry marked historically approved does not imply that routine prescribing and supply remain available in 2026.
profiles.mechanism: PTH activates PTH1 receptors in renal and skeletal tissue. It promotes calcium retention in the kidney, increases phosphate excretion, and stimulates production of active vitamin D. Bone effects depend on the timing and intensity of exposure: physiologic replacement, intermittent anabolic therapy, and chronic excess are not biologically equivalent. Full-length PTH and the active 1–34 fragment share receptor activity but differ in molecule, formulation, and clinical evidence.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Full-length PTH replacement has clinical evidence in hypoparathyroidism, but Natpara’s manufacturing and supply history is essential context. Current PTH analogs require separate evaluation; a shared hormone pathway does not make products interchangeable.

sections.title: Historical approved use
sections.body: Natpara was approved to help control hypocalcemia in hypoparathyroidism as an adjunct to calcium and vitamin D. Because of potential osteosarcoma risk, its label reserved treatment for patients inadequately controlled with conventional therapy. This indication differs from using a PTH analog to build bone in osteoporosis.

sections.title: The REPLACE trial
sections.body: The randomized REPLACE study examined whether recombinant PTH(1–84) could reduce oral calcium and active vitamin D requirements while maintaining calcium control. More treated participants achieved the combined endpoint than placebo recipients. This provides clinical replacement evidence, but does not prove that all symptoms or long-term renal complications resolve.

sections.title: Safety during treatment and transitions
sections.body: Important risks include severe hypercalcemia, severe hypocalcemia when treatment is interrupted, hypersensitivity, and digoxin interactions. The historical label carried a boxed osteosarcoma warning based on animal findings and required a restricted program. Transitioning away from a PTH product requires a supervised mineral-management plan because supplements alone may need substantial adjustment.

sections.title: What happened to Natpara?
sections.body: Takeda’s announcement attributes discontinuation to unresolved product-specific supply issues and describes continued supply only while remaining inventory permits. Manufacturing cessation is separate from the hormone’s established physiology or the efficacy of other approved PTH products. The later long-acting product palopegteriparatide should be read under its own profile and current label.

sections.title: Does Natpara’s discontinuation mean all PTH replacement stopped?
sections.body: No. Natpara is a specific recombinant PTH(1–84) product affected by manufacturing and supply problems. Other PTH-based medicines have separate development programs and approvals. Their availability, indications and safety instructions must be checked individually; the disappearance of one product does not establish equivalence of another.

profiles.name: Pasireotide
profiles.summary: Pasireotide is an approved somatostatin analog for selected pituitary hormone-excess disorders. It can reduce ACTH-driven cortisol production in Cushing’s disease and, in its long-acting formulation, treat acromegaly, but hyperglycemia and diabetes are prominent treatment concerns.
profiles.description: Signifor and Signifor LAR contain pasireotide with different delivery profiles. The immediate-release product is approved for adults with Cushing’s disease when pituitary surgery is unsuitable or not curative. The depot product also has an acromegaly indication after inadequate surgery or when surgery is not an option. Cushing’s disease specifically refers to pituitary ACTH-driven cortisol excess and should not be confused with every form of Cushing’s syndrome. The desired hormonal response can improve illness while simultaneously creating new metabolic problems, so benefit is assessed together with glucose control and other safety measures.
profiles.mechanism: Pasireotide binds several somatostatin receptor subtypes, with strong activity at SSTR5, which is frequently expressed by corticotroph pituitary tumors. Suppressing ACTH can lower adrenal cortisol secretion. In acromegaly, inhibition of GH secretion reduces downstream IGF-1. Its broader receptor profile differs from octreotide and lanreotide, and suppression of insulin-related pathways contributes to the notable hyperglycemia risk.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Pasireotide is a specialist option for selected pituitary disease, with a meaningful tradeoff between hormone control and metabolic toxicity. Product formulation, cortisol or IGF-1 response and glucose monitoring must be considered together.

sections.title: Disease and formulation boundaries
sections.body: Cushing’s disease treatment is aimed at a pituitary source of ACTH excess. The long-acting formulation also treats specified acromegaly populations. Neither is a general treatment for stress-associated cortisol variation or an unexplained abnormal hormone test.

sections.title: Cortisol-control evidence
sections.body: The pivotal Cushing’s study assessed urinary free cortisol and clinical changes. Some patients achieved biochemical control, but response was not universal and was influenced by baseline disease severity. That supports monitored treatment rather than an expectation of guaranteed normalization.

sections.title: Metabolic and cardiac concerns
sections.body: Hyperglycemia may appear soon after initiation and can require diabetes treatment. The labels also address bradycardia, QT prolongation, liver-test abnormalities, gallstones and gastrointestinal symptoms. Excess cortisol suppression can produce adrenal insufficiency.

sections.title: Assessing both benefit and burden
sections.body: Glucose, HbA1c, liver tests, ECG-related risk and electrolytes are relevant before and during therapy. Hormone response and symptoms are followed alongside adverse effects. New steatorrhea or weight loss can indicate pancreatic exocrine insufficiency.

sections.title: Why somatostatin analogs differ
sections.body: Pasireotide, lanreotide and octreotide share a family relationship but have different receptor profiles and approved roles. One agent’s glucose effects or tumor evidence should not be assumed for another, and depot formulations require their own prescribing instructions.

profiles.name: Pegcetacoplan
profiles.molecularClass: PEG-conjugated cyclic peptide complement C3 inhibitor
profiles.summary: Pegcetacoplan inhibits complement C3 and is approved in different formulations for distinct diseases. Systemic Empaveli treats PNH and specified complement-associated kidney diseases; intravitreal Syfovre treats geographic atrophy secondary to age-related macular degeneration. Their routes, outcomes, and major safety concerns differ substantially.
profiles.description: Pegcetacoplan acts relatively early in the complement cascade, affecting both C3-related processes and downstream terminal complement activity. This supports several disease-specific uses. Empaveli is administered subcutaneously for adult paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and, under current US labeling, C3 glomerulopathy or primary immune-complex membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis from age 12 to reduce proteinuria and loss of kidney function. Syfovre is a separate eye-injection product for geographic atrophy associated with age-related macular degeneration. A shared active ingredient does not make the products interchangeable. Systemic complement suppression and local ocular administration create different benefits, monitoring needs, and serious risks.
profiles.mechanism: Pegcetacoplan binds complement C3 and C3b, reducing activation and generation of downstream effectors. In PNH, this can limit both C3-mediated extravascular red-cell destruction and terminal-complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis. In complement-associated kidney disease, it reduces pathway activity implicated in glomerular injury. Local ocular complement inhibition aims to slow geographic-atrophy lesion growth. The mechanism does not restore tissue already lost to retinal degeneration.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Pegcetacoplan has several established, formulation-specific indications. Empaveli’s systemic infection precautions and Syfovre’s ocular risks must remain separate, and slowing geographic-atrophy progression should not be represented as restoring lost vision.

sections.title: Systemic indications and evidence
sections.body: Empaveli treats adult PNH and specified C3G or primary IC-MPGN patients aged 12 and older. In PNH, the PEGASUS trial showed improved hemoglobin compared with continued eculizumab in selected patients with persistent anemia. Kidney evidence has its own population and outcomes; it should not be inferred solely from PNH results.

sections.title: What the eye product can do
sections.body: Syfovre is injected into the eye for geographic atrophy secondary to AMD. Its clinical program showed slower growth of atrophic lesions. This is a disease-progression endpoint, not proof of regenerated retina or restored visual acuity. The eye product is neither a substitute for systemic Empaveli nor an injection for all forms of macular disease.

sections.title: Two different safety contexts
sections.body: Systemic Empaveli carries a boxed warning and REMS for serious infections caused by encapsulated bacteria; vaccination does not eliminate risk. Syfovre warnings include endophthalmitis, retinal detachment, retinal vasculitis or vascular occlusion, neovascular AMD, inflammation, and increased eye pressure. These require formulation-specific assessment rather than one generic safety list.

sections.title: Why does the kidney indication need current labeling?
sections.body: Pegcetacoplan’s approved uses have expanded since its original PNH approval. Current Empaveli labeling includes reduction of proteinuria and loss of kidney function for specified C3G and primary IC-MPGN populations. A dated source limited to PNH or only proteinuria can therefore omit a relevant current indication; transplant subgroups still have specific evidence limits.

profiles.name: Pegvisomant
profiles.summary: Pegvisomant is an approved medicine that blocks growth-hormone action in acromegaly. Unlike GH replacement or GH-releasing peptides, it reduces downstream IGF-1 signaling; follow-up emphasizes IGF-1, liver function, glucose and the underlying pituitary tumor rather than GH concentration alone.
profiles.description: Somavert is used in acromegaly when surgery or radiotherapy has been inadequate or is unsuitable. The medicine acts outside the pituitary by blocking GH receptors in target tissues, so it can reduce IGF-1 even when GH secretion remains elevated. That distinction explains why biochemical monitoring differs from treatment that suppresses hormone release. Pegvisomant does not directly remove a pituitary tumor, and ongoing assessment of the underlying lesion remains part of care. It is not a peptide for increasing growth, athletic performance or muscle mass; its intended action is to oppose excessive GH signaling.
profiles.mechanism: Pegvisomant is an engineered GH analog with polyethylene-glycol modification that binds the GH receptor without producing normal receptor activation. It competitively blocks endogenous GH signaling, reducing hepatic and tissue responses including IGF-1 production. This may improve insulin sensitivity in patients with GH excess. Standard GH measurements can be misleading during treatment because pegvisomant may interfere with assays and does not suppress secretion in the same way as pituitary-directed drugs.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Pegvisomant treats excess GH action by blocking its receptor. A falling IGF-1 can show benefit even without a falling GH result, while liver safety, glucose changes and pituitary follow-up remain necessary.

sections.title: Where it fits in acromegaly care
sections.body: The label covers patients with inadequate response to surgery or radiation, or for whom these treatments are inappropriate. The goal is normalization of IGF-1, rather than use for nonspecific symptoms attributed to hormone imbalance.

sections.title: Receptor-blockade efficacy
sections.body: A randomized trial demonstrated dose-related reduction and normalization of IGF-1 in acromegaly. This established the ability to block peripheral GH effects, a different therapeutic strategy from inhibiting GH secretion at the pituitary.

sections.title: Liver and injection-site effects
sections.body: Liver enzyme elevations and liver injury require attention to label-based monitoring. Systemic hypersensitivity and injection-site changes, including lipohypertrophy, can occur. Improved insulin sensitivity may increase hypoglycemia risk in patients receiving glucose-lowering medicines.

sections.title: Why GH is not the response target
sections.body: The label directs assessment using IGF-1. GH assay interference and ongoing endogenous GH secretion make GH concentration unsuitable as the sole efficacy marker. Monitoring of pituitary tumor size remains relevant because receptor blockade is not direct tumor removal.

sections.title: Opposite direction from GH replacement
sections.body: Somatropin supplies GH activity, while pegvisomant blocks it. Their structural relationship does not imply similar therapeutic goals. A peptide catalog should preserve that opposite action rather than grouping both under an undifferentiated growth-hormone benefit.
