profiles.name: Pemvidutide
profiles.molecularClass: Dual GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist peptide
profiles.summary: Pemvidutide is an investigational metabolic peptide studied for obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. In a phase 2b MASH trial, it improved the inflammation-resolution endpoint at twenty-four weeks but did not significantly improve the separate fibrosis endpoint at that time.
profiles.description: Pemvidutide, formerly ALT-801, is designed to combine GLP-1 and glucagon receptor activity. Its liver program distinguishes fat reduction, resolution of steatohepatitis and improvement in scarring because these are related but different outcomes. IMPACT enrolled patients with biopsy-confirmed MASH and moderate-to-advanced fibrosis. The published interim analysis supports activity against MASH, while the negative fibrosis comparison remains important. Marketing language that says a peptide 'reverses fatty liver' can obscure these distinctions, the investigational status and the need for longer follow-up to evaluate clinical consequences.
profiles.mechanism: GLP-1 signaling influences appetite and glucose regulation, while glucagon receptor activity changes hepatic metabolism and can increase energy expenditure. The combined design aims to reduce body weight and liver fat without losing glycemic control. Reduced hepatic fat may contribute to improvement in inflammation, but remodeling established fibrosis is a separate biological process and must be measured directly rather than assumed from weight loss.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Pemvidutide has promising human MASH evidence with a clearly mixed endpoint result. It remains investigational, and improvement in liver inflammation should not be described as established reversal of fibrosis or cirrhosis.

sections.title: Who was studied
sections.body: IMPACT enrolled 212 patients with biopsy-confirmed MASH and stage F2 or F3 fibrosis. It did not establish treatment for all causes of elevated liver enzymes, all degrees of fibrosis or decompensated cirrhosis.

sections.title: Positive MASH endpoint
sections.body: At twenty-four weeks, MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis occurred in 58% and 52% of the two active groups versus 20% with placebo. The prespecified analysis supported a treatment effect on that endpoint.

sections.title: Fibrosis result was different
sections.body: Fibrosis improvement without worsening MASH occurred in 33% and 36% of the active groups versus 28% with placebo; neither comparison was statistically significant. The study therefore did not meet both primary endpoints at the reported time point.

sections.title: Tolerability and remaining uncertainty
sections.body: Most adverse events were mild or moderate, and discontinuation because of adverse events was uncommon in the reported study. Longer exposure and larger populations remain necessary to characterize rare harms and the clinical importance of histologic changes.

sections.title: Why several liver measures are needed
sections.body: Body weight, imaging-derived liver fat, liver enzymes, inflammation and fibrosis answer different questions. Earlier metabolic studies support development, but a favorable change in one measure cannot be substituted for proven reduction in liver failure, transplantation or mortality.

profiles.name: Pentapeptide-18
profiles.summary: Pentapeptide-18 is a cosmetic ingredient associated with Leuphasyl and expression-line claims. Small formulation studies and laboratory or computational research exist, but they do not establish equivalence to botulinum toxin. Evidence should distinguish the peptide from retinol-containing combinations and delivery technologies.
profiles.description: Pentapeptide-18 is discussed as an enkephalin-inspired peptide intended for cosmetic modulation of expression-related lines. The commercial name Leuphasyl appears in older publications that use inconsistent peptide numbering, making identity checks important. Its evidence base includes a small volunteer formulation study, newer combinations with retinol, and molecular modeling. These study types answer different questions. A docking calculation does not measure wrinkle reduction, and a retinol-containing product can improve appearance without demonstrating that every added peptide contributes. Interpreting the evidence therefore requires knowing what was tested, rather than assuming that a mechanistic story guarantees a visible effect.
profiles.mechanism: The proposed rationale involves modulation of neuronal signaling through an enkephalin-like concept, potentially reducing expression-related activity. This remains a cosmetic mechanistic hypothesis requiring evidence of relevant exposure in intact skin. A 2026 spectroscopic and computational study examined molecular properties and interactions; such work can generate hypotheses but cannot establish clinical neuromuscular inhibition, superiority to another treatment, or a durable cosmetic benefit.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Pentapeptide-18 has preliminary cosmetic research, with substantial attribution and study-design limits. Molecular modeling, small uncontrolled studies, and retinol combinations should not be presented as independent proof of a Botox-equivalent effect.

sections.title: The small early volunteer study
sections.body: A 2014 report tested Leuphasyl-containing emulsions in twenty volunteers over two months and tracked facial lines with an imaging method. Its small size and lack of a clearly described matched placebo design limit causal interpretation. It provides preliminary product observations rather than robust evidence of isolated-peptide efficacy or equivalence to injected neuromodulators.

sections.title: Combination and computational work
sections.body: A 2024 study evaluated retinol and pentapeptide-18 in lipid-nanocarrier formulations. The delivery system and retinol are active parts of the intervention, so improvement cannot all be credited to the peptide. A 2026 structural and molecular-interaction paper supplies a different kind of evidence and should not be counted as another clinical wrinkle trial.

sections.title: Keep the intended use and uncertainty clear
sections.body: Cosmetic status is not FDA drug approval. Small volunteer studies cannot reliably detect rare reactions or define long-term exposure. Tolerability belongs to the finished product and delivery method, and topical research does not establish an injectable use or an anxiety, pain, or neurological indication.

profiles.name: Petrelintide
profiles.summary: Petrelintide is an investigational amylin analog for obesity with positive phase 2 results. It targets appetite through a pathway different from GLP-1-only medicines, but its weight-loss, gastrointestinal tolerability and long-term outcome evidence are still developing.
profiles.description: Formerly ZP8396, petrelintide is being developed by Zealand Pharma and Roche as a long-acting amylin-based obesity treatment. The ZUPREME-1 study evaluated adults without type 2 diabetes over forty-two weeks, while other studies address diabetes and potential combinations. The program is clinically substantive, but a phase 2 result does not establish the full benefit-risk profile or imply that every amylin analog behaves alike. In particular, petrelintide, cagrilintide and pramlintide differ in molecule, duration, formulation and approved or investigational purpose, so their evidence should not be pooled into one product claim.
profiles.mechanism: Amylin is a pancreatic peptide involved in satiation and meal-related regulation. Petrelintide is engineered to extend amylin-related receptor signaling and reduce food intake with prolonged exposure. This mechanism offers a route to appetite regulation that does not require GLP-1 agonism in the same molecule. Clinical trials are needed to determine whether the design produces a useful balance of weight reduction and tolerability.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Petrelintide has encouraging phase 2 obesity evidence, including a potentially useful tolerability profile, but remains investigational. Comparisons with established medicines require direct studies and a fuller long-term safety record.

sections.title: Development population
sections.body: ZUPREME-1 enrolled adults with obesity or qualifying overweight without type 2 diabetes. Separate development addresses adults with diabetes and combinations. These populations should remain distinct when presenting expected outcomes.

sections.title: Phase 2 weight results
sections.body: The study randomized 493 participants, with 485 exposed to treatment. Mean weight reduction continued through forty-two weeks, reaching up to 10.7% in the reported efficacy analysis. The analysis assumed a particular treatment-adherence scenario rather than predicting every real-world outcome.

sections.title: What favorable tolerability means
sections.body: Nausea was more frequent with petrelintide than placebo; vomiting was uncommon, and diarrhea and constipation rates were relatively similar. This is an encouraging study-specific pattern, not evidence of no gastrointestinal effects or proof of superiority to another agent.

sections.title: Questions phase 2 cannot settle
sections.body: The trial was not designed to establish reductions in cardiovascular events or mortality. Longer-term persistence, uncommon harms and effects in more diverse populations remain relevant, even when average weight reduction and short-term tolerability look favorable.

sections.title: Next-stage interpretation
sections.body: Roche and Zealand describe continued development, including plans for later-stage studies and combinations. Company announcements are useful for program status but should be identified separately from peer-reviewed clinical findings and final regulatory decisions.

profiles.name: Plecanatide
profiles.molecularClass: Uroguanylin analog and GC-C agonist peptide
profiles.summary: Plecanatide is an oral peptide that increases intestinal fluid secretion to treat chronic idiopathic constipation and IBS with constipation in adults. It acts locally in the gut, but can cause severe diarrhea and has strict pediatric safety restrictions.
profiles.description: Trulance is used for two adult constipation diagnoses: chronic idiopathic constipation and irritable bowel syndrome with constipation. The first centers on persistent difficult or infrequent bowel movements without an identified secondary cause; IBS-C also includes a pattern of abdominal pain. Plecanatide does not treat mechanical obstruction and is not established as a general gut-healing or anti-inflammatory medicine. Its limited systemic absorption is relevant to pharmacology, but the clinically important effect is movement of fluid into the intestine, which can become excessive in susceptible patients.
profiles.mechanism: Plecanatide resembles the endogenous peptide uroguanylin and activates guanylate cyclase-C on intestinal epithelial cells. Increased cyclic GMP stimulates chloride and bicarbonate secretion, principally through CFTR, increasing luminal fluid and transit. Animal findings also link extracellular cyclic GMP to reduced pain-nerve activity. Clinical improvement in IBS-C is evaluated by patient symptoms and bowel outcomes rather than that laboratory mechanism alone.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Plecanatide is an established adult constipation treatment with a specific local mechanism. Its favorable absorption profile does not remove the need to assess diarrhea, dehydration, obstruction and pediatric restrictions.

sections.title: Two adult indications
sections.body: U.S. labeling covers chronic idiopathic constipation and IBS-C in adults. Safety and effectiveness below age eighteen are not established. Eligibility is based on the constipation diagnosis, not simply a desire to improve digestion or bowel frequency.

sections.title: Clinical trial outcomes
sections.body: A phase 3 placebo-controlled trial in chronic idiopathic constipation assessed sustained complete spontaneous bowel-movement response. Plecanatide improved that endpoint, supporting a measurable bowel-function benefit rather than a claim that it corrects every underlying cause of constipation.

sections.title: Diarrhea and dehydration
sections.body: Diarrhea is the common adverse reaction and can be severe. The label includes a boxed warning for serious dehydration risk in pediatric patients. Minimal measurable drug in the circulation does not prevent dehydration caused by its local intestinal effect.

sections.title: Pediatric and obstruction restrictions
sections.body: Plecanatide is contraindicated below age six and in known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction. The label advises avoiding use from six to under eighteen because pediatric safety and effectiveness have not been established.

sections.title: Relationship to linaclotide
sections.body: Both medicines activate intestinal GC-C, but they are different peptides with different product labels. In particular, current linaclotide pediatric approvals should not be transferred to plecanatide merely because the two drugs share a receptor target.

profiles.name: PN-943
profiles.molecularClass: Oral gastrointestinal-restricted α4β7 integrin antagonist peptide
profiles.summary: PN-943 is an investigational oral peptide designed to block gut-directed immune-cell trafficking in ulcerative colitis. Its phase 2 study missed the prespecified primary endpoint, with an exploratory signal at the lower exposure; it is distinct from predecessor PTG-100.
profiles.description: The development concept is local intestinal activity with low systemic exposure. PN-943 binds α4β7 integrin, a target also used by an approved antibody medicine, but that shared target does not establish equivalent efficacy or safety. Healthy-volunteer studies supported oral stability and target engagement. The IDEAL phase 2 study then tested clinical remission in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. Its higher-exposure primary comparison was negative, while the lower group showed a numerical signal. The sponsor subsequently prioritized other programs and stated that it would not commit further internal development resources beyond completing the extension.
profiles.mechanism: α4β7 integrin helps leukocytes interact with MAdCAM-1 and traffic to intestinal tissue. PN-943 is designed to inhibit that interaction and related immune-cell activation while remaining largely within the gastrointestinal compartment. Low measured plasma exposure is consistent with this design, but it does not by itself prove adequate tissue effect or absence of systemic biological consequences. Receptor occupancy is a pharmacodynamic marker, not clinical remission.
profiles.keyTakeaway: PN-943 provides proof-of-concept research for an oral gut-restricted approach, with a mixed clinical result and an inactive internal development commitment. It should not be described as approved oral vedolizumab or merged with PTG-100.

sections.title: What healthy-volunteer studies showed
sections.body: Phase 1 studies found low systemic exposure and measurable target engagement, with generally favorable short-term tolerability. These findings supported testing in ulcerative colitis but could not establish clinical efficacy in inflamed bowel.

sections.title: IDEAL results
sections.body: The sponsor reported 159 evaluable patients. The higher trial group did not separate from placebo on the prespecified primary endpoint. The lower group had 27.5% clinical remission versus 14.5% with placebo, a numerical difference that did not reach conventional statistical significance in the overall analysis.

sections.title: Do not substitute a predecessor study
sections.body: PTG-100 is a related predecessor, not another name for PN-943. Results from PTG-100 cannot be assigned directly to PN-943. Similarly, efficacy of an approved injectable α4β7 antibody validates the target’s relevance without validating this oral molecule.

sections.title: What remains unresolved
sections.body: Early tolerability and low plasma exposure do not establish long-term safety in active inflammatory bowel disease, combination therapy or pregnancy. A complete clinical benefit-risk profile would require successful confirmatory development and broader exposure.

sections.title: Program status
sections.body: In its third-quarter 2022 update, Protagonist stated that it intended to dedicate no further internal clinical or manufacturing-development resources after completing the IDEAL extension. The record is therefore research history, not evidence of an approved or continuously advancing phase 3 product.

profiles.name: Polymyxin B / Colistin
profiles.molecularClass: Related cyclic lipopeptide antibiotics; colistimethate is a colistin prodrug
profiles.summary: Polymyxin B and colistin are related antibiotics used against susceptible Gram-negative bacteria, including some highly resistant infections. They damage bacterial membranes but can also injure kidneys and the nervous system. Colistimethate is a prodrug of colistin, so the products are not interchangeable.
profiles.description: This grouped entry covers both polymyxin B and colistin while retaining the differences that matter clinically. Polymyxin B is administered as an active antibiotic; many systemic colistin products contain colistimethate sodium, which is converted into active colistin. Formulation, conversion, exposure, and dose-expression conventions differ. These older antibiotics regained importance as resistance narrowed treatment options, but their toxicity makes them specialist tools rather than routine broad-spectrum wellness antimicrobials. Topical combination products containing polymyxin B also exist and must not be confused with systemic injection products. Selection depends on the actual pathogen, susceptibility, infection site, kidney function, and available alternatives.
profiles.mechanism: Polymyxins interact with lipid components of Gram-negative bacterial outer membranes and disrupt membrane integrity, producing bactericidal activity. Their cationic peptide and lipid portions are both important to this interaction. Colistimethate must first convert to active colistin, whereas polymyxin B is supplied in active form. This chemical difference influences how exposure develops and why a treatment plan cannot be transferred by simply substituting one product name for the other.
profiles.keyTakeaway: These are established but potentially toxic antibiotics for defined susceptible infections. Correctly distinguishing polymyxin B, colistin, and colistimethate is essential, and neither their peptide structure nor laboratory activity makes them a general infection-prevention strategy.

atAGlance.label: Members covered
atAGlance.value: Polymyxin B and colistin / polymyxin E

sections.title: What each member contributes
sections.body: Polymyxin B injection and colistimethate injection have labels for susceptible Gram-negative infections. Susceptibility is not universal across Gram-negative species, and resistance testing matters. Their use against difficult resistant pathogens is an infection-specific decision; evidence of activity against one organism cannot establish effectiveness against an unrelated infection or at a poorly reached site.

sections.title: Why formulation is part of the evidence
sections.body: Coly-Mycin M contains colistimethate and expresses potency in terms of colistin base activity, while other jurisdictions or products may use different conventions. Polymyxin B has its own labeling. Studies, exposure targets, and safety observations must be attached to the actual formulation; the class relationship does not make preparation or unit conventions equivalent.

sections.title: Kidney, nerve, and respiratory risks
sections.body: Both medicines carry substantial renal and neurologic safety concerns. Neuromuscular blockade can cause respiratory weakness or paralysis, especially with interacting medicines or vulnerable patients. Colistimethate labeling also describes renal tubular electrolyte disturbances. Monitoring and review of other nephrotoxic or neurotoxic exposures are central to systemic treatment.

sections.title: Is polymyxin in an ointment the same treatment?
sections.body: No. A skin, ear, or eye combination product delivers different exposure and has different indications from systemic therapy. Conversely, an injectable product is not a substitute for a topical formulation. The shared ingredient name does not establish route interchangeability, adequate tissue exposure, or comparable risks.

profiles.name: Pramlintide
profiles.summary: Pramlintide is an approved adjunct to mealtime insulin for selected adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. It complements insulin’s actions but increases the risk of severe hypoglycemia, especially in type 1 diabetes, and is not an approved standalone obesity medicine.
profiles.description: Symlin replaces selected actions of amylin, a hormone normally released with insulin from pancreatic beta cells. Its indication concerns people using mealtime insulin who have not achieved desired glycemic control despite optimized insulin treatment. The therapy adds complexity because meals, insulin exposure, glucose monitoring and gastric emptying all interact. The label emphasizes careful patient selection and trained diabetes follow-up. This is a distinct clinical role from newer long-acting amylin analogs being developed for obesity. Their mechanism-related relationship does not permit transfer of approvals, administration practices or safety assumptions.
profiles.mechanism: Pramlintide slows gastric emptying, suppresses inappropriate post-meal glucagon secretion and promotes satiety. These actions reduce the rate at which glucose enters the circulation after meals and complement the glucose-disposal effect of insulin. Because carbohydrate appearance and insulin action can become mismatched, adding pramlintide without an appropriate prescribing plan can cause severe hypoglycemia. Delayed gastric emptying can also affect oral-drug absorption.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Pramlintide is an established but selective adjunct to insulin, requiring coordinated glucose management. Its amylin mechanism does not make it an interchangeable weight-loss peptide or eliminate the risks of concomitant insulin.

sections.title: Who the label describes
sections.body: The indication includes type 1 or type 2 diabetes with mealtime insulin when desired control remains unmet despite optimal insulin therapy. The label stresses suitability, reliable monitoring and access to experienced diabetes care.

sections.title: What clinical benefit is measured
sections.body: Registration studies assessed additional glycemic improvement with insulin-based treatment, along with body-weight effects. A weight change in diabetes trials does not establish an independent obesity indication or demonstrate long-term cardiovascular benefit.

sections.title: Hypoglycemia and nausea
sections.body: Severe hypoglycemia is the major boxed risk, particularly in type 1 diabetes. Nausea is common. Reduced awareness of low glucose and confirmed gastroparesis are contraindications, because they increase the difficulty or danger of coordinating treatment with meals and insulin.

sections.title: Why it is kept separate from insulin
sections.body: The label prohibits mixing pramlintide and insulin in the same injection because this can alter pharmacokinetics. It also addresses oral medicines for which prompt absorption or a threshold concentration is important, given delayed gastric emptying.

sections.title: Relationship to investigational amylin drugs
sections.body: Cagrilintide and petrelintide are different long-acting analogs with separate obesity-development programs. Pramlintide’s approval does not approve those molecules, and their trial results do not establish a new indication for Symlin.

profiles.name: Retatrutide
profiles.molecularClass: Triple GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor agonist peptide
profiles.summary: Retatrutide is an investigational triple-receptor metabolic peptide with substantial weight-loss effects in randomized trials, including phase 3 results. It remains distinct from approved semaglutide and tirzepatide products; trial efficacy does not establish an approved retail product or long-term outcomes for every population.
profiles.description: Developed as LY3437943, retatrutide combines GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor activity in one molecule. Its clinical program evaluates obesity and associated metabolic complications. The 2026 TRIUMPH-1 publication extends the evidence beyond the earlier phase 2 study, including outcomes in participants with knee osteoarthritis or obstructive sleep apnea. These findings come from regulated studies using controlled manufacturing and follow-up. Products sold online under the same name are not the studied product by default. As of this review, the ingredient remains investigational rather than an FDA-approved weight-management medicine.
profiles.mechanism: GIP and GLP-1 activity influence glucose-dependent insulin secretion and appetite, while glucagon receptor activity adds effects on hepatic metabolism and energy expenditure. The design balances pathways that do not have identical effects on glucose or food intake. Calling it a triple agonist describes receptor pharmacology; it does not establish that three targets are always safer or clinically superior to two for an individual patient.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Retatrutide has progressed to compelling phase 3 evidence, but remains an investigational medicine at this review date. Efficacy, regulatory approval, manufacturing quality and long-term safety are separate questions.

sections.title: Conditions under investigation
sections.body: The program studies obesity and associated conditions rather than a nonspecific wellness effect. TRIUMPH-1 included adults with obesity without diabetes and prospectively assessed weight and selected knee-osteoarthritis and sleep-apnea outcomes.

sections.title: What the 2026 phase 3 study found
sections.body: Across 2,339 randomized participants, the highest trial group had a mean 25.0% weight reduction at eighty weeks versus 3.9% with placebo in the treatment-regimen analysis. Pain and sleep-apnea outcomes also improved in relevant subgroups. These are group averages under a specified estimand.

sections.title: Observed tolerability and remaining uncertainty
sections.body: Gastrointestinal adverse events were common. The earlier phase 2 trial also observed dose-related heart-rate increases that peaked and later declined. Larger trials improve confidence but cannot fully characterize rare events or risks after many years of use.

sections.title: Why headline percentages can mislead
sections.body: Phase 2 and phase 3 studies differed in duration, participants and analysis. Comparing their percentages with another drug’s separate trial is not equivalent to a randomized head-to-head comparison. Discontinuation handling also affects reported weight-loss estimates.

sections.title: Trial evidence versus approved access
sections.body: FDA communications identify retatrutide among unapproved products marketed for weight loss. A research-use label, compounded presentation or online certificate does not turn an investigational molecule into an approved medicine or validate a seller’s clinical claims.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Does a positive phase 3 trial mean retatrutide is approved? No. Trial results and regulatory authorization are separate milestones, and the current FDA source identifies it as unapproved.

Can its headline weight loss be directly compared with another medicine's trial? Differences in populations, duration and handling of discontinuation can change estimates; direct comparative studies provide stronger evidence for treatment rankings.

profiles.name: Rusfertide
profiles.summary: Rusfertide is now an FDA-approved treatment for erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera, marketed as Mimrylo. It mimics hepcidin to restrict iron availability for red-cell production. Approval in August 2026 supersedes older descriptions that list it only as investigational.
profiles.description: Polycythemia vera is a myeloproliferative disease in which excessive red-cell production can require repeated therapeutic phlebotomy and other treatment. Rusfertide targets iron regulation rather than directly eliminating the underlying abnormal cell clone. By mimicking hepcidin, it reduces the iron supply available for erythropoiesis and helps control hematocrit. Earlier REViVE findings led to the phase 3 VERIFY program and US approval of Mimrylo on August 28, 2026. Its approved indication is erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera. This should not be broadened to general blood donation replacement, every cause of high hematocrit, iron overload, or treatment of anemia.
profiles.mechanism: Rusfertide inhibits ferroportin, the transporter that moves iron from cells into circulation, reproducing a central action of endogenous hepcidin. Reduced iron availability to the marrow limits red-cell production and lowers hematocrit. This is iron redistribution and restriction of erythropoiesis, not destruction of mature red cells. The mechanism also explains why blood counts and anemia require monitoring and why the drug does not itself eradicate the PV clone.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Rusfertide has moved from clinical development into approved US care for a specific PV indication. Its benefit is hematocrit control and reduced phlebotomy burden; platelet increases, anemia, injection reactions, and continuing disease management still matter.

sections.title: From REViVE to VERIFY
sections.body: REViVE showed improved hematocrit control and reduced phlebotomy requirements, including a randomized withdrawal comparison. The phase 3 VERIFY study evaluated rusfertide added to ongoing standard care in adults requiring repeated phlebotomy. The approved label describes the controlled results supporting use; improvement in these endpoints is not the same as proof of curing PV.

sections.title: A current approval, not just a trial candidate
sections.body: FDA approved Mimrylo for erythrocytosis in adults with polycythemia vera on August 28, 2026. Earlier references correctly described development at their publication dates but are outdated if presented as current status. The indication remains specific to PV-related erythrocytosis rather than all disorders of iron or red-cell production.

sections.title: Platelets and anemia require attention
sections.body: Current labeling warns about new or worsening thrombocytosis and calls for blood-count monitoring. Injection-site reactions and anemia were common adverse reactions in the clinical program. Embryo-fetal toxicity is another warning. Hematocrit improvement therefore needs to be considered alongside platelets, symptoms, other PV therapy, and the overall treatment plan.

sections.title: Does it eliminate the need for other PV care?
sections.body: Not necessarily. The pivotal trial allowed ongoing standard treatment, and rusfertide targets erythrocytosis through iron regulation rather than removing the underlying neoplastic clone. A reduction in phlebotomy burden does not establish that every patient can stop cytoreductive therapy or that long-term thrombotic risk has been eliminated.

profiles.name: Secretin
profiles.molecularClass: Synthetic human secretin diagnostic peptide hormone
profiles.summary: Secretin is an approved diagnostic hormone used to stimulate pancreatic or gastrin secretion during selected tests and procedures. It helps evaluate pancreatic exocrine function, investigate gastrinoma and identify pancreatic duct openings; it is not routine treatment for digestive insufficiency.
profiles.description: ChiRhoStim supplies synthetic human secretin, a hormone normally involved in the response to acidic intestinal contents. Its diagnostic value comes from provoking a measurable pancreatic or gastrin response. The product can assist pancreatic exocrine-function assessment, gastrinoma evaluation and identification of the ampulla or accessory papilla during ERCP. These uses depend on technique and clinical context. The current label cautions that medicines and underlying conditions can blunt or exaggerate responses, so an abnormal result should not be interpreted without understanding how the test was prepared, performed and measured.
profiles.mechanism: Secretin stimulates pancreatic duct cells to release bicarbonate-rich fluid, helping neutralize acidic contents entering the intestine. Receptor signaling opens pathways including CFTR-mediated secretion, with neural contributions also described. In gastrinoma, an abnormal gastrin response can become a diagnostic signal. The hormone therefore acts as a controlled physiologic stimulus; the measurement and interpretation, not lasting hormone replacement, are the purpose of the approved procedure.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Secretin is useful in specific diagnostic pathways when test conditions are controlled. A stimulated secretion measurement does not independently diagnose every pancreatic disorder or establish a therapeutic role for repeated secretin administration.

sections.title: Approved diagnostic applications
sections.body: The label covers stimulation of pancreatic secretion to aid diagnosis of exocrine dysfunction, stimulation of gastrin to aid gastrinoma diagnosis, and pancreatic secretion to help locate duct openings during ERCP.

sections.title: Technique is part of the test
sections.body: Label-described studies compared synthetic and biologically derived secretin preparations and assessed pancreatic responses. The label notes variation between investigators and laboratories, so reference values and operator proficiency matter to interpretation.

sections.title: Adverse effects observed during testing
sections.body: In the label-described open-label trial of 531 patients, reported reactions included nausea, vomiting, flushing and upset stomach. Most patients received a single administration. These observations characterize diagnostic exposure and do not establish the safety of repeated administration for unapproved therapeutic purposes.

sections.title: Medication-related diagnostic errors
sections.body: Anticholinergic medicines can blunt pancreatic response. Proton-pump inhibitors and H2 blockers can alter gastrin responses and falsely suggest gastrinoma. Test preparation should follow the supervising clinician’s plan rather than unsupervised withdrawal of necessary medicines.

sections.title: Underlying disease can distort response
sections.body: Prior vagotomy or inflammatory bowel disease can reduce responses, while alcoholic or other liver disease may increase pancreatic secretion enough to mask coexisting pancreatic disease. Additional clinical assessment can therefore be necessary even after a technically completed test.

sections.title: Diagnostic secretion is not pancreatic replacement
sections.body: Secretin briefly stimulates a response for measurement or visualization. It does not supply digestive enzymes, restore destroyed pancreatic tissue or establish treatment for chronic abdominal symptoms. Those clinical goals require separate evidence and evaluation.

profiles.name: Selank
profiles.summary: Selank is a research peptide investigated for anxiety-related effects. A small human comparison with medazepam and laboratory studies provide preliminary information, but they do not establish broad anxiety treatment efficacy or long-term safety. U.S. approval has not been established.
profiles.description: Selank is a modified peptide related to tuftsin, an endogenous immune-associated sequence. It appears in discussions of anxiety, stress, and cognition, but those labels span different scientific questions. The available human literature includes relatively small studies in selected clinical populations. A study comparing two active treatments can be informative, yet without a placebo group it may not separate drug effects from expectation, symptom fluctuation, and other care. Claims of a universally effective, non-sedating, dependence-free anxiolytic go beyond what these reports can establish. The compound and its acetate form also require attention to formulation and characterization.
profiles.mechanism: Research has explored enkephalin metabolism, gene-expression changes, and pathways related to inhibitory neurotransmission. These are proposed or experimentally observed effects, not proof of one fully established clinical mechanism. A blood enkephalin marker does not directly measure brain anxiety circuits. Mechanistic observations may guide future studies, but the relationship between exposure, symptom relief, and adverse effects remains insufficiently characterized.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Selank’s small clinical reports justify further investigation, not certainty about efficacy or safety. Anxiety outcomes, sedation, dependence potential, interactions, and long-term exposure each require evidence rather than assumptions based on a peptide’s proposed mechanism.

atAGlance.label: Evidence limitation
atAGlance.value: No placebo in the cited comparison

atAGlance.label: Safety issue
atAGlance.value: Limited human characterization of compounded forms

sections.title: The small comparative study
sections.body: A 2008 report included 62 patients with generalized anxiety disorder or neurasthenia: 30 received Selank and 32 medazepam. The authors reported similar anxiolytic effects and examined serum enkephalin activity. The small sample, mixed diagnostic population, and active-comparator design limit certainty. Similar scores in one study do not establish equivalence to standard treatments across broader populations.

sections.title: Laboratory results remain a separate evidence tier
sections.body: An original rat study examined expression of genes involved in neurotransmission after Selank exposure. Such work helps formulate hypotheses about action but cannot demonstrate clinical benefit or freedom from dependence. Molecular changes can be complex and may have different consequences depending on dose, tissue, route, and disease context.

sections.title: Formulation and regulatory limits
sections.body: FDA identifies safety-information gaps for compounded Selank acetate and possible immunogenicity related to aggregation or impurities. This concern is about insufficient characterization, not a measured incidence of harm. A compounding discussion or a research sale does not create an approved U.S. anxiety indication.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
sections.body:
Does similar performance to medazepam prove that Selank is equivalent?
No. One small active-comparator study cannot establish broad clinical equivalence, particularly without a placebo group and a robust equivalence design.

Does the available evidence establish no dependence or interaction risk?
No. Those claims require specific, adequately designed human studies. Small anxiety reports and laboratory gene-expression changes do not answer every safety question.

profiles.name: Selepressin
profiles.molecularClass: Synthetic selective vasopressin V1a-receptor agonist peptide
profiles.summary: Selepressin is an investigational vasopressin analog designed to emphasize vascular V1a-receptor activity. It was studied as an alternative pressor strategy in septic shock. The major SEPSIS-ACT trial stopped for futility and did not improve its primary patient-centered outcome, so a routine treatment role is unestablished.
profiles.description: Vasopressin affects both vascular tone and kidney water retention through different receptors. Selepressin was designed to favor the vascular V1a pathway and avoid some V2-mediated effects. This supplied a rationale for investigating whether more selective signaling could reduce organ support needs in septic shock. The development program progressed beyond small hemodynamic experiments to the adaptive SEPSIS-ACT randomized trial. That study tested a meaningful combined outcome of days alive and free of ventilation and vasopressors. Its negative result is central to the profile and cannot be replaced by an assumption that receptor selectivity must produce a clinical advantage over existing vasopressor care.
profiles.mechanism: Selepressin stimulates V1a receptors on vascular smooth muscle, increasing vascular tone through intracellular calcium signaling. Relative V1a selectivity was intended to separate pressor effects from V2-associated water retention and other vasopressin actions. However, a cleaner receptor profile does not automatically improve survival or organ recovery. Vasoconstriction may still alter regional perfusion, and the clinical consequence depends on illness, exposure, and concomitant treatment.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Selepressin remains an experimental vasopressor with a negative major outcome trial. Its receptor selectivity explains the development rationale but does not establish superiority, a survival benefit, or an approved alternative to vasopressin.

atAGlance.label: Trial outcome
atAGlance.value: Stopped for futility; primary endpoint not improved

sections.title: What the adaptive trial found
sections.body: SEPSIS-ACT treated 828 participants and stopped after its first part for futility. Selepressin did not significantly improve ventilator- and vasopressor-free days compared with placebo added to background care. The trial also did not show significant benefit in key secondary outcomes including 90-day mortality or kidney-replacement-therapy-free days.

sections.title: Why the endpoint is more informative than pressure alone
sections.body: The protocol was designed to test whether a pressor strategy translated into less organ support while accounting for death. That is a broader clinical question than whether the drug can raise arterial pressure. The adaptive design allowed early termination when the probability of success was inadequate, limiting unnecessary further exposure.

sections.title: Selective receptors do not remove ischemic concerns
sections.body: Cardiac arrhythmia and ischemic events were monitored in the trial, including cardiac, mesenteric, and peripheral ischemia. Event comparisons did not establish a decisive clinical advantage. The monitored intensive-care setting and short exposure also limit conclusions about any unrelated outpatient or chronic use.

sections.title: Is it an approved replacement for vasopressin?
sections.body: No. The reviewed development program does not establish an approved US selepressin medicine or routine septic-shock indication. Vasopressin’s approval and familiarity cannot be transferred to this modified analog. Any future role would require new evidence addressing a specific population and clinically meaningful outcomes.

profiles.name: Semaglutide
profiles.summary: Semaglutide is an established prescription GLP-1 medicine with formulation-specific roles in type 2 diabetes, weight management, cardiovascular risk reduction, kidney protection and selected liver disease. Benefits and eligibility depend on the actual approved product, rather than the ingredient name alone.
profiles.description: Semaglutide appears in Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy, but these products have different evidence, indications and delivery systems. Current Wegovy labeling includes injectable and oral formulations for adult weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction in eligible patients; the injection also has pediatric obesity and selected MASH indications. Ozempic has diabetes, cardiovascular and kidney-outcome indications in defined adult populations. Oral absorption depends on the formulation, so tablet and injectable amounts are not interchangeable. This is a medicine for diagnosed conditions with ongoing follow-up, not evidence that semaglutide benefits every person seeking metabolic optimization.
profiles.mechanism: Semaglutide activates the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor. It increases insulin secretion and lowers glucagon when glucose is elevated, influences appetite and food intake, and delays gastric emptying. Structural changes and albumin binding prolong exposure compared with the short-lived natural hormone. Appetite reduction contributes substantially to weight loss, while clinical trials establish specific cardiovascular and kidney benefits that cannot be inferred from weight change alone.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Semaglutide has strong clinical evidence, but its benefits must be matched to the formulation and patient population studied. The current label, medical history and treatment goals determine suitability.

sections.title: Approved uses and product differences
sections.body: Wegovy injection includes obesity treatment from age 12 and, in adults, noncirrhotic MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis under accelerated approval. Oral Wegovy has adult weight and cardiovascular indications. Ozempic’s current label includes adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.

sections.title: What the major trials show
sections.body: STEP 1 established substantial weight reduction in adults without diabetes. SELECT demonstrated fewer major cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. These were different populations and endpoints; one result should not be substituted for another.

sections.title: Adverse effects and important exclusions
sections.body: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation are common. Labels address pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, dehydration-related kidney injury, severe gastrointestinal reactions and aspiration during anesthesia. Semaglutide is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2; the thyroid warning originates in rodent findings.

sections.title: What follow-up considers
sections.body: Diabetes treatment may require attention to hypoglycemia when insulin or insulin secretagogues are also used. Retinopathy history, kidney function during dehydration, gastrointestinal tolerance and pregnancy plans affect clinical management. Product switching requires a prescribing plan because exposure and indications differ.

sections.title: What accelerated MASH approval means
sections.body: The MASH indication was supported by improvement in liver inflammation and fibrosis. Continued approval may depend on confirmation of clinical benefit. This does not establish reversal of cirrhosis or suitability for every cause of abnormal liver tests.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.body:
Are Ozempic and Wegovy interchangeable? They contain the same active ingredient, but their approved indications, formulations and instructions differ. Product-specific information remains necessary.

Does a weight-management approval also establish every liver benefit? No. Wegovy's MASH indication concerns a defined noncirrhotic population and uses an accelerated approval pathway; it is not an approval for every fatty-liver condition.

profiles.name: Semax
profiles.summary: Semax is an experimental peptide with laboratory neurobiology research and limited clinical reports, particularly from Russian neurological settings. These studies do not establish routine cognitive enhancement. FDA’s 2026 review found insufficient evidence for proposed neurological uses in U.S. compounding.
profiles.description: Semax contains the sequence Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro and is described in the literature as an ACTH-fragment analog. Its relationship to a hormone fragment does not make it equivalent to full-length ACTH or establish an endocrine replacement role. Research has explored stroke recovery, optic-nerve disorders, brain-network changes, and neurochemical effects. The reports vary substantially in size, controls, and endpoints. A small imaging experiment or a change in a blood biomarker answers a different question from whether a treatment improves disability or daily function. That distinction is essential when evaluating claims about memory, concentration, or neurological recovery.
profiles.mechanism: Preclinical studies have examined monoamine signaling and neurotrophic or inflammatory pathways. A rodent study found changes in serotonin-related measurements and interactions with amphetamine-related dopamine effects. Such findings demonstrate biological activity in the experimental setting, not a predictable cognitive benefit in humans. A mechanism can also introduce interaction questions; it should not be presented only as a list of potential advantages.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Semax has biological activity and limited human research, but reliable clinical benefit remains uncertain for the proposed U.S. uses. Brain imaging, BDNF changes, and animal behavior cannot substitute for robust patient-centered trials.

sections.title: Clinical reports require careful interpretation
sections.body: A 1997 stroke report compared 30 Semax-treated patients with 80 controls receiving conventional therapy. A later rehabilitation study assessed functional measures and plasma BDNF. These reports are relevant signals, but their designs and reporting do not provide the same certainty as a large, rigorously blinded, placebo-controlled program. They do not establish enhancement in healthy users.

sections.title: A biomarker is not a treatment outcome
sections.body: Rodent neurotransmitter experiments can help generate hypotheses about how Semax acts. They cannot establish an effective or safe human intervention. Similarly, an imaging-network change may occur without a meaningful improvement in symptoms, independence, or quality of life; those outcomes need direct assessment.

sections.title: U.S. review and unresolved safety
sections.body: FDA’s 2026 compounding evaluation addressed cerebral ischemia, migraine, and trigeminal neuralgia and found insufficient evidence to support effectiveness. It also described safety limitations. The briefing is not a marketing authorization or a final regulatory determination. Injectable and intranasal preparations should not be treated as interchangeable evidence categories.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
sections.body:
Do BDNF or brain-imaging changes prove better cognition?
No. Biomarkers and imaging can show biological activity without demonstrating improved memory, independence, or quality of life. Those outcomes require direct clinical assessment.

Did the 2026 FDA compounding review approve Semax?
No. The briefing was a scientific evaluation for an advisory process, not a marketing authorization. It described important efficacy and safety limitations.

profiles.name: Sermorelin
profiles.summary: Sermorelin stimulates the pituitary to release growth hormone. Geref products had US approvals for pediatric growth hormone deficiency and diagnostic testing before discontinuation. Modern compounded wellness products do not inherit those approvals, and pediatric growth findings do not establish anti-aging or weight-loss benefits in healthy adults.
profiles.description: Sermorelin reproduces the biologically active first 29 amino acids of growth hormone-releasing hormone with an amidated terminus. Its historical pharmaceutical uses included testing pituitary GH reserve and treating selected children with growth failure caused by GH deficiency. Geref was discontinued, and FDA later determined that removal from sale was not for safety or effectiveness reasons. That history is more precise than describing all sermorelin as either never approved or currently approved for wellness. Contemporary compounded preparations have their own quality and evidence questions. Trials of tesamorelin, a different GHRH analog used in HIV-associated lipodystrophy, cannot substitute for sermorelin-specific outcome evidence.
profiles.mechanism: Sermorelin binds GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotroph cells and stimulates endogenous GH release. The response requires functioning pituitary tissue and is shaped by somatostatin and normal endocrine feedback. GH can then increase hepatic and tissue IGF-1 production. This differs from injecting GH directly, but preservation of feedback does not by itself establish clinical superiority or exclude adverse effects from altering the GH–IGF-1 axis.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Sermorelin has a genuine historical clinical role, but the current product and indication must be identified. Compounded anti-aging treatment is not equivalent to the discontinued Geref approvals or to trials of other GHRH analogs.

atAGlance.label: Historical uses

atAGlance.label: FDA finding
atAGlance.value: Not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons

sections.title: The pediatric evidence
sections.body: A multicenter open-label study enrolled 110 previously untreated prepubertal children with GH deficiency. Growth velocity increased during treatment, with 86 children included in the efficacy analysis. The design and selected population matter: this was not a placebo-controlled longevity trial or evidence that healthy adults benefit from raising GH.

sections.title: Why the approval history needs qualification
sections.body: FDA records identify distinct diagnostic and pediatric Geref approvals. The manufacturer discontinued both presentations, and approvals were withdrawn in 2009. FDA’s 2013 determination found that their removal from sale was not for safety or effectiveness reasons. This does not create an approved indication for contemporary compounded weight-loss or anti-aging regimens.

sections.title: What remains uncertain in wellness use
sections.body: The pediatric study reported generally favorable tolerability, but its size, duration, and patient selection cannot define long-term risk in healthy older adults. An endocrine response should be interpreted alongside glucose metabolism, symptoms, and the reason GH testing was undertaken. Compounded product composition and sterility are additional questions beyond the molecule’s historical evidence.

sections.title: Are tesamorelin results evidence for sermorelin?
sections.body: No. Both stimulate the GHRH receptor, but they differ in structure, exposure, approved use, and trial populations. Reduced visceral fat in a tesamorelin trial cannot be relabeled as a sermorelin result. Clinical claims should cite the actual molecule, formulation, population, and outcome studied.

profiles.name: Setmelanotide
profiles.summary: Setmelanotide targets a central appetite pathway in specific rare forms of obesity. Current U.S. approval includes acquired hypothalamic obesity and defined syndromic or genetic conditions, with different minimum ages. It is not approved for ordinary polygenic obesity.
profiles.description: Imcivree is used when a defined disruption of hypothalamic appetite signaling makes MC4 receptor activation an appropriate therapeutic target. The 2026 U.S. label includes acquired hypothalamic obesity from age four, and Bardet-Biedl syndrome or qualifying POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency from age two. Genetic findings require appropriate interpretation; a benign variant or a commercial genetic result alone is not sufficient. Diagnosis and clinical context distinguish this treatment from broader obesity medicines. Its evidence should therefore be understood in relation to the specific disorder rather than body weight alone.
profiles.mechanism: Setmelanotide activates melanocortin-4 receptors in brain pathways regulating hunger, satiety and energy expenditure. It can restore downstream signaling when certain upstream pathways are impaired. Activity at melanocortin-1 receptors explains increased skin pigmentation. This targeted biology is why the medicine can help selected rare disorders while the label does not expect the same effectiveness in unrelated genetic syndromes or general polygenic obesity.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Setmelanotide is a precision treatment for specified causes of obesity. The 2026 acquired-hypothalamic-obesity indication is a real expansion, but it does not make the medicine suitable for all obesity.

sections.title: Current indication boundaries
sections.body: Acquired hypothalamic obesity, Bardet-Biedl syndrome and qualifying POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency are separate labeled groups. The label excludes general polygenic obesity and deficiencies based on variants classified as benign or likely benign.

sections.title: Rare-disease trial evidence
sections.body: Trials in POMC and LEPR deficiency measured body-weight reduction and hunger in small, genetically defined groups. The results support targeted treatment, but small rare-disease cohorts cannot be treated as evidence for the much larger population with common obesity.

sections.title: Pigmentation, mood and sexual effects
sections.body: Generalized darkening of skin, changes in moles and new pigmented lesions require attention. Depression or suicidal thoughts, spontaneous erections and other sexual adverse reactions have occurred. Serious hypersensitivity is possible.

sections.title: Additional considerations in acquired hypothalamic obesity
sections.body: The current label adds attention to acute adrenal insufficiency and sodium disturbances in patients with acquired hypothalamic obesity, especially those with central diabetes insipidus. These problems reflect the broader endocrine consequences of hypothalamic disease.

sections.title: What the diagnosis contributes
sections.body: A specialist assessment connects the clinical syndrome, genetic or structural findings, hunger pattern and other pituitary deficits. The decision is not based on a weight threshold alone, and skin examination and mental-health follow-up remain part of the treatment context.

profiles.name: Sincalide
profiles.summary: Sincalide is an intravenous diagnostic peptide that contracts the gallbladder and stimulates pancreatic secretion in defined testing settings. It helps clinicians measure digestive-organ function or facilitate imaging; it is not an established treatment for chronic gallbladder disease or general digestive wellness.
profiles.description: Kinevac reproduces selected actions of cholecystokinin, the hormone released after food enters the intestine. Its U.S. label includes stimulating gallbladder contraction, pancreatic secretion when used with secretin, and accelerating movement of a barium meal in selected examinations. The resulting response is measured under a diagnostic protocol. Symptoms, imaging findings and test technique determine interpretation. A low or high measured response is not a complete diagnosis on its own, and the same drug can produce different discomfort or gallbladder measurements when the administration protocol changes.
profiles.mechanism: The active octapeptide corresponds to the biologically active end of cholecystokinin. It stimulates gallbladder smooth-muscle contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion, and affects gastrointestinal motility. Those normal digestive responses become a controlled challenge during testing. Contracting a gallbladder that contains stones can also cause stone movement, which is why the diagnostic purpose does not eliminate the possibility of biliary complications.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Sincalide is a diagnostic challenge agent with useful but protocol-dependent responses. It should be understood as part of a supervised investigation, not as a gallbladder cleanse or a long-term digestive treatment.

sections.title: Approved diagnostic purposes
sections.body: The label covers gallbladder contraction, pancreatic secretion in conjunction with secretin, and selected barium-meal transit applications in adults. These are procedural uses, not an approval for treating unexplained abdominal pain with repeated peptide exposure.

sections.title: Why administration protocol matters
sections.body: A multicenter investigation of gallbladder ejection-fraction testing compared sincalide infusion approaches and established reference values for a standardized method. The study illustrates that a numeric test result is meaningful only in relation to how the test was performed.

sections.title: Adverse effects and exclusions
sections.body: Abdominal cramping, nausea and other gastrointestinal symptoms can occur. Serious allergic reactions are possible, including reactions related to sulfites in the preparation. Intestinal obstruction and hypersensitivity to sincalide or relevant components are contraindications.

sections.title: Gallstones and pregnancy
sections.body: Gallbladder contraction can dislodge stones and contribute to obstruction. The label also addresses possible pregnancy-related effects because stimulation can affect smooth muscle. These risks belong in the decision to perform the test, not only in interpreting the result.

sections.title: What a test can establish
sections.body: A functional measurement can support a diagnosis when combined with symptoms and structural imaging. It does not by itself demonstrate that surgery, supplements or another particular intervention will resolve a patient’s symptoms.

profiles.name: Somapacitan
profiles.summary: Somapacitan is a long-acting growth-hormone analog used for adult GH deficiency and specified pediatric growth disorders. Current U.S. labeling extends beyond pediatric GH deficiency to selected small-for-gestational-age, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short-stature populations from age two and a half.
profiles.description: Sogroya provides prolonged GH activity through a modified molecule that binds albumin. Its adult indication is replacement in established growth-hormone deficiency. The current pediatric label includes growth failure from inadequate GH secretion, certain children born small for gestational age without catch-up growth, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short stature. These are defined clinical diagnoses, not a general indication to increase height or improve body composition in otherwise healthy people. Weekly administration changes convenience and exposure patterns, but does not remove the endocrine evaluation, growth assessment or safety surveillance required for GH-directed treatment.
profiles.mechanism: Somapacitan activates GH receptors in target tissues and stimulates downstream effects, including IGF-1 production. Reversible albumin binding prolongs exposure compared with unmodified somatropin. Some actions are mediated through IGF-1, while others reflect direct GH signaling. Because concentrations and IGF-1 vary across the weekly interval, the timing of biochemical assessment matters when interpreting response and avoiding excessive hormonal exposure.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Somapacitan is established long-acting GH therapy for labeled deficiencies and growth conditions. Its expanded pediatric scope should be recognized, while healthy-adult anti-aging and unrestricted height-enhancement claims remain outside that evidence.

sections.title: Current approved populations
sections.body: The 2026 label includes pediatric GH deficiency, selected SGA short stature, Noonan syndrome and idiopathic short stature from age 2.5, plus adult GH deficiency. The actual diagnostic criteria and growth-plate status determine eligibility.

sections.title: How adult and pediatric benefit differ
sections.body: The adult REAL-1 study evaluated body-composition and metabolic effects in GH deficiency. Pediatric studies assess annualized height velocity and growth outcomes against daily somatropin. Adult fat-mass findings and childhood linear growth are not interchangeable endpoints.

sections.title: GH-related adverse effects
sections.body: Fluid retention, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension and thyroid or adrenal-axis changes require attention. Pediatric monitoring includes hip or knee pain suggesting slipped capital femoral epiphysis and progression of scoliosis. Hypersensitivity can occur.

sections.title: Important restrictions
sections.body: Active malignancy, certain acute critical illnesses, severe diabetic retinopathy and closed growth plates for pediatric growth promotion are contraindications. Specific respiratory-risk restrictions apply to children with Prader-Willi syndrome, although that syndrome is not a general Sogroya growth indication.

sections.title: Weekly GH is not a direct volume substitution
sections.body: Long-acting GH analogs differ from daily somatropin and from each other. Their exposure patterns and IGF-1 interpretation are product-specific, so a change in formulation requires a clinical plan rather than simple conversion by injection volume.

profiles.name: Somatropin (rhGH)
profiles.summary: Somatropin is recombinant human growth hormone with established, product-specific indications in GH deficiency and selected growth or wasting conditions. It is not an approved general anti-aging treatment, and excess exposure can cause metabolic, fluid-retention and growth-related complications.
profiles.description: Somatropin products supply a recombinant form of human GH. Several brands treat pediatric growth disorders and adult GH deficiency, while specialized products have other indications: Serostim treats HIV-associated wasting, and Zorbtive has a short-bowel-syndrome indication. Those indications belong to the relevant product labels rather than every somatropin presentation. In children, diagnosis, remaining growth potential and exclusion of alternative causes determine treatment. In adults, a symptom such as fatigue or an age-related decline in a hormone measurement is not by itself established GH deficiency. The full endocrine context matters.
profiles.mechanism: Somatropin activates GH receptors and stimulates IGF-1 production, affecting linear growth, protein synthesis, lipid metabolism and body composition. It also has direct metabolic actions, including reduced insulin sensitivity in some settings. Replacing deficient hormone can be beneficial, but pharmacologic excess is biologically different from replacement. The same growth signaling that supports treatment explains concerns about tumor activity and inappropriate use after growth plates have closed.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Somatropin is a family of established hormone medicines with product-specific uses. Deficiency treatment, pediatric growth care, HIV wasting and short-bowel therapy should remain distinct from unsupported healthy-adult rejuvenation claims.

sections.title: Approval depends on the product
sections.body: Genotropin covers adult GH deficiency and specified pediatric disorders. Serostim covers adult HIV wasting with antiretroviral therapy. Zorbtive’s short-bowel indication is another distinct use. Sharing somatropin does not make every branded indication interchangeable.

sections.title: What meaningful response looks like
sections.body: Pediatric care assesses height velocity and growth potential; adult replacement evaluates deficiency-related clinical and biochemical outcomes. In HIV wasting, body weight, lean mass and physical endurance are relevant. A higher IGF-1 alone is not a universal measure of improved health.

sections.title: Important adverse effects
sections.body: Edema, joint or muscle symptoms, carpal-tunnel-type symptoms, glucose intolerance and intracranial hypertension can occur. Treatment may reveal or alter thyroid and adrenal deficits. Pediatric monitoring also addresses slipped capital femoral epiphysis and scoliosis progression.

sections.title: Malignancy and critical illness
sections.body: Active malignancy, certain acute critical illnesses and severe diabetic retinopathy are important contraindications. Growth promotion is inappropriate after epiphyseal closure. Specific airway and respiratory restrictions apply in Prader-Willi syndrome because of reported sudden deaths in high-risk children.

sections.title: Why wellness claims require separate evidence
sections.body: The benefits of replacing a deficient hormone do not establish benefits from raising it above physiological need. Approved disease-specific experience cannot be converted into a claim that somatropin prolongs life or safely improves appearance in healthy adults.

profiles.name: Survodutide
profiles.molecularClass: Dual glucagon and GLP-1 receptor agonist peptide
profiles.summary: Survodutide is an investigational dual glucagon/GLP-1 agonist with clinical programs in obesity and MASH. Phase 2 liver and phase 3 obesity findings support further development, while gastrointestinal tolerability and the distinction between weight, inflammation and fibrosis outcomes remain important.
profiles.description: Known during development as BI 456906, survodutide combines two receptor activities in a long-acting peptide. Its development includes obesity trials in people with and without diabetes and liver studies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis. SYNCHRONIZE-1 results reported in 2026 provide phase 3 obesity evidence, moving beyond the earlier proof-of-concept studies. That progress does not itself establish marketing approval. The liver and obesity programs also answer separate questions: a reduction in body weight or liver fat is not automatically proof of improved fibrosis, prevention of cirrhosis or fewer cardiovascular events.
profiles.mechanism: GLP-1 receptor activity affects appetite, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and gastric emptying. Glucagon receptor activity adds hepatic and energy-expenditure effects. Survodutide’s design seeks to combine these actions into useful weight and liver responses while balancing glucose regulation. Because receptor balance, exposure and patient population differ among dual agonists, findings for another GLP-1/glucagon peptide cannot substitute for survodutide-specific trials.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Survodutide has advanced clinical evidence for obesity and MASH but remained investigational at this review. Benefits should be stated for the specific trial endpoint, with tolerability and long-term clinical uncertainty included.

sections.title: Distinct development programs
sections.body: Obesity studies assess weight change and related outcomes, while MASH studies evaluate liver disease directly. Eligibility and background disease differ, so the programs should not be combined into a single undifferentiated metabolic-benefit claim.

sections.title: MASH phase 2 findings
sections.body: A randomized liver trial found greater improvement in MASH without worsening fibrosis with survodutide than placebo. This supports activity on the prespecified histologic endpoint; it does not by itself demonstrate prevention of liver failure or a survival benefit.

sections.title: Phase 3 obesity evidence
sections.body: The 2026 SYNCHRONIZE-1 report describes greater body-weight reduction than placebo in adults with obesity without diabetes. The published study and sponsor announcement should be interpreted using their specified analysis and population, rather than informal cross-trial rankings.

sections.title: Tolerability considerations
sections.body: Gastrointestinal adverse events were prominent in clinical development. Treatment discontinuation and exposure escalation affect both tolerability and reported efficacy. Larger studies and follow-up are needed to clarify uncommon risks and long-term use in patients with multiple comorbidities.

sections.title: What remains to be established
sections.body: Positive late-stage results are part of an approval submission, not a final authorization. At this review date, survodutide is retained as investigational; the evidence does not validate a research supplier’s product or a self-directed combination with other metabolic medicines.

profiles.name: TB-500
profiles.molecularClass: Ambiguous commercial name; often an acetylated seven-amino-acid thymosin beta-4 fragment
profiles.summary: TB-500 is a commercial designation often used for a short fragment of thymosin beta-4, but some sellers use it for the full-length molecule. Human efficacy for the fragment is not established. Evidence from full-length thymosin beta-4 eye or wound studies cannot be transferred to it.
profiles.description: The identity problem is central to understanding TB-500. An analytical study identified N-terminally acetylated residues 17–23 of thymosin beta-4, Ac-LKKTETQ, in a product sold under this name. FDA discusses the LKKTETQ fragment separately from the full 43-amino-acid peptide. Commercial use of TB-500 is inconsistent, so the name alone does not specify what is in a vial. Marketing commonly invokes tendon healing, injury recovery, angiogenesis, or muscle repair, but a plausible relationship to a natural repair-associated molecule does not establish a safe clinical treatment. This profile treats the fragment as distinct from the separate thymosin beta-4 entry.
profiles.mechanism: The fragment overlaps an actin-interacting region of thymosin beta-4, which helps explain interest in cell movement and tissue repair. However, a short sequence cannot be assumed to reproduce the structure, intracellular distribution, processing, or biological actions of the full peptide. A validated human therapeutic mechanism for injected TB-500 has not been established; fragment identity and formulation must be resolved before mechanistic or outcome claims can be evaluated.
profiles.keyTakeaway: TB-500 requires exact identity checks and conservative evidence interpretation. The fragment lacks established human therapeutic benefit, and published full-length thymosin beta-4 studies do not validate commercial TB-500 injections or recovery claims.

sections.title: What does the name actually identify?
sections.body: Mass-spectrometric characterization of a TB-500 preparation found an acetylated thymosin beta-4 fragment. This demonstrates the identity of that analyzed material, not every modern product carrying the name. Full-length thymosin beta-4, non-acetylated LKKTETQ, and acetylated LKKTETQ should be kept separate in a scientific record rather than treated as guaranteed synonyms.

sections.title: Why parent-peptide trials are not fragment trials
sections.body: A small ophthalmic study used full-length thymosin beta-4 as RGN-259 in patients with neurotrophic keratopathy. It did not test TB-500 fragment injections for tendon or muscle recovery. Different sequence, route, formulation, and disease each limit evidence transfer. The clinical result should remain attached to the product actually studied.

sections.title: What FDA says about the fragment
sections.body: FDA identifies possible immune reactions arising from aggregation or peptide impurities and states that it has not identified adequate human exposure information for the fragment. This is an evidence gap, not a demonstrated safe dose. Uncertain product identity makes adverse-effect prediction even harder when preparations are sourced outside pharmaceutical research.

sections.title: Does being a piece of a natural peptide make it safe?
sections.body: No. Fragmentation and acetylation can change biological activity, persistence, and immune recognition. Natural production of the parent molecule also differs from administering a manufactured preparation systemically. The available sources do not establish TB-500 as a treatment for tendon tears, muscle injury, chronic pain, or general recovery.

profiles.name: Teduglutide
profiles.summary: Teduglutide is an approved intestinal-rehabilitation medicine for short bowel syndrome in patients who depend on parenteral support. It improves absorptive capacity and can reduce support requirements, while requiring surveillance for intestinal growth, obstruction, fluid overload and biliary or pancreatic complications.
profiles.description: Gattex is used in adults and children aged one year and older with short bowel syndrome who require parenteral support. The clinical problem is loss of enough functioning bowel to maintain fluid or nutrition without intravenous assistance. Treatment aims to improve absorption and reduce that dependence under specialist management. Some patients become independent of support, but that is not guaranteed, and anatomy and baseline needs influence response. Teduglutide is not approved for routine IBS, nonspecific intestinal permeability, or recovery from ordinary digestive discomfort, despite being described as a gut-directed peptide.
profiles.mechanism: Teduglutide activates the GLP-2 receptor and promotes intestinal adaptation, including changes in mucosal growth and absorption. A substitution makes it more resistant to enzymatic breakdown than native GLP-2. Increased absorption can improve fluid and nutrient handling, but can also alter exposure to oral medicines and create fluid overload if parenteral support is not reassessed. Its growth-promoting biology explains the attention to intestinal neoplasia.
profiles.keyTakeaway: Teduglutide can reduce the burden of parenteral support in established intestinal failure. Its benefits depend on coordinated nutritional care and surveillance; they should not be generalized into a claim of universal gut repair.

atAGlance.label: Age scope
atAGlance.value: 1 year and older in the U.S.

sections.title: The condition it treats
sections.body: Short bowel syndrome with dependence on parenteral support is the labeled condition. The objective is improved intestinal absorption and reduced support needs, not simply a change in stool frequency or an improvement in a nonspecific digestive symptom score.

sections.title: Reduction in support requirements
sections.body: Clinical trials and their extensions measured reductions in parenteral-support volume and days of support. Some participants achieved enteral autonomy over extended treatment. These outcomes require careful accounting of fluid and nutrition rather than interpreting weight gain alone as recovery.

sections.title: Growth-related and gastrointestinal risks
sections.body: The label warns about possible acceleration of neoplastic growth, intestinal obstruction and gallbladder, biliary or pancreatic disease. Baseline and follow-up gastrointestinal surveillance are part of the treatment framework, with age-specific recommendations.

sections.title: Fluids and other medicines
sections.body: Greater absorption can cause fluid overload or worsen heart failure if support is not adjusted. It can also increase absorption of oral drugs, especially important for medicines with a narrow therapeutic range. Changes or discontinuation require reassessment of fluid and electrolyte balance.

sections.title: Why specialist nutrition care remains necessary
sections.body: A lower prescribed support volume is beneficial only if hydration, kidney function, nutritional status and daily function remain adequate. Teduglutide supports intestinal rehabilitation; it does not replace the ongoing assessment of the remaining bowel and overall nutritional needs.
